And you know, guys like Seaquin, guys like Bon, guys like Ash and Jensy, you know, all those guys can do that. And um, you know, I'm no different. I'm going to come into this league and I'm going to put a lot of emphasis on making sure that we can extend drives, we can, you know, finish when we get down in the red zone. Um, and that's what makes a a running back great. You know, a running back is supposed to make the the the defense rest longer and it's supposed to make uh the offense, you know, score touchdowns. you know, obviously, you know, block and allow guys like Marv to, you know, run those deep balls and allow a quarterback to throw that deep ball and he can get that and get a touchdown, but running backs are very crucial for um a team success and that's why it's, you know, very important to have a good one. So, I feel very honored to um be drafted as high as I was. There's a lot of responsibility that comes with that. Like I think Spider-Man said, with great power comes great responsibility. So, um I am going to make sure that I uphold to that legacy and uh of of having a good running back and allowing them to have uh a lot of team to have great success and I'm going to come in and work to do that. You know, I'm I'm ready to work. Glad to be here and like I said, we're going to do some great things in in Arizona. >> Jeremiah, you mentioned at the very beginning kind of the the impact of your family support system, your parents both being police officers, being raised in that environment. I guess kind of how what impact has that had on you growing up and and how has that translated to the person that you are today? >> Yes. So, my parents, you know, being police officers, they were uh they're army veterans as well. So, um you can only imagine what that household was like. It wasn't very, [laughter] you know, you can only imagine, man. I mean, that my dad, you know, wasn't very strict, but he made sure I was doing the right things at all times. You know, my mom was the same way. Um, you know, they were they enforced the law, so they enforced rules in the house. You know, I couldn't do certain things, but all those things got me to being here today. Um, you know, they instilled principles of discipline in me. Um, my dad always talks about consistently as a man, he always talks about word is bond. So, um, I mean, as a as a man today and as a as a player today, I'm very disciplined. You know, I got a D3 from my from my uh running back coach, Coach Dean McCulla, being detailed, dependable, and disciplined. So, I try to live by those principles, you know, every single day and um they're always going to stick with me for the rest of my life. But my parents are the first ones that that instilled those principles in me. And um that's allowed me to be the player I am today. >> Jeremiah Bob McMahon of Arizona Republic. Uh welcome. Back to Spider-Man for a minute. Um [laughter] you were shy and introverted as a young young man, young a young kid. Where did how much strength did you find from that selfisolation and and your alter ego? You you're already writing about it, creating it. Uh and in the Jer Monster, can you talk about that path in your life? >> Yeah, of course. So, um Jerem is a comic that I released uh past this past October and I literally did no work on it. My dad right here did all the work. Made sure I had a great team surrounding me that made sure I was being portrayed in a right. in the right way. So that's Jerem. Um but I mean, you know, me being an introvert, so you say. Um this just allowed me to be me, you know, at all times. You know, I'm I'm I'm a to myself guy, um when I choose to be, but I can also be a guy that that connects with people. Um I got a, you know, on and off switch. I can do both. But um me being, you know, in the house and just being to myself, you know, growing up has allowed me to just be authentically me. And I feel like um a lot of kids growing up should, you know, invest in themselves and get to know themselves because at the end of the day, you are all you got in this world. So um yeah, man, invest in yourself and and and find out who you are. And that's what I did at a young age, which is allowed me to be myself. And uh yeah.

title: Why the Cardinals Took Jeremiyah Love at No. 3 | GM Monti Ossenfort Sits Down With Dani Sureck
text: A loud eruption out of the draft room, the Cardinals stick and pick at number three. It's running back Jeremiah Love out of Notre Dame. Right to my left, general manager Monti Ossenfort got to make that exciting, life-changing phone call. I am Dani Soreck. Monti, you said you can never take too many good players in the draft. What made Jeremiah Love the best player at three? Yeah, Dani, I think really the the way he's been an explosive playmaker for Notre Dame the last two years. And not only just as a runner, uh but also as a receiver. Um his ability to put stress on the defense, um and score the ball from just about anywhere. You we saw short, tough, physical runs. We saw him uh break away in space and make long, explosive runs. And then really an underrated part of his game is really his pass protection. You don't see as many uh you don't see many uh college running backs at all come out and be as detailed as he is in pass protection. So, his ability to be on the field for all three downs just really attracted us to him. The numbers are impressive. Averaged almost seven yards a carry each of the last two seasons. Last year, 21 total touchdowns, a Heisman finalist. You mentioned the pass protection. What else do you like most about Love's game that you don't see on the stat sheet? Yeah, really. I mean, I it's you see guys that are um that are as fast as he is and explosive as he is, but he does still get the tough yards. He he churns out those, you know, third and three, third and four yard runs, finishes his runs. Um sometimes you can see guys like him uh choose the path of least resistance, go out of bounds. So, you know, Jeremiah does not like to go out of bounds. And so, um and it's not surprising once you get to know the kid and see what he's about and his makeup, um you know, it's it's not surprising that he plays the way he does. Your years of scouting experience, when it comes to running backs who are successful, productive in college, which traits most easily transfer into the pros early on? Yeah, it's really uh you know, the ability to run with strength, balance, uh vision, instincts, um you know, the the holes that that are there in college, they get a lot tighter in the NFL. And so, when you see backs that are able to uh keep their speed, keep their acceleration, their quickness even on contact, um those are guys that tend to translate well to our level. It's a fine line of best player available and position of need. You have a full running backs room right now. Where did Jeremiah Love fit in that realm and where do you envision his role becoming? Yeah, I mean, really at this point Jeremiah's role will be whatever he makes of it. And so, we'll get him in here. His first job will be learning this coaches, learning his teammates, uh learning the new offensive system, and then just to get out on the field with his teammates and compete. And it's it's it's it's amazing how many times competition sorts itself out. Um you know, Jeremiah brings a unique skill set to the room uh that's different than the other guys in our room. And there's those things will all sort themselves out. We'll put the players in the best position to succeed and to help the team. I'm really excited to get him here to carve out that role. Over the last few years, you've taken a lot of pride in making that life-changing phone call to the player surrounded by their friends and family. Once you got the right phone number to get in contact with Love, what was your message to him telling him he's a Cardinal? >> Yeah, it's just it's it's a surreal moment, you know, I can't I can't imagine how those those kids feel when they get, you know, something that they've worked their whole life for. Um and just to feel uh feel them on the phone and feel like a sense of joy, relief, uh it all is mixed into one. And so, um just to be able to share that moment with them uh knowing that their family is there and and just the elation that they must be feeling. Uh it's it's just a really cool moment. >> Character is a high value for you. You've met with Love throughout this process. What will fans soon learn about Love and the type of person he is? >> Yeah, he's a really impressive kid. I mean, he's he's humble, uh his head's on his shoulders the right way. Um he's about the right stuff. It's team first. He wants to do whatever he can do to help the team. Uh I can't wait for you guys to get a chance to meet him. Uh he's a he's a really cool kid and and we're just lucky to have it to add him to our group. >> Cardinals fans are very excited about the new addition to this team. Congratulations, Monti. Appreciate the time. Cardinals fans, for more coverage on Jeremiah Love as well as the rest of the draft, stay locked in on azcardinals.com. For Monti Ossenfort, I'm Dani Soreck. Thanks so much for tuning in.

title: GM Monti Ossenfort And HC Mike LaFleur Address The Media After Day 1 Of NFL Draft | AZ Cardinals
text: Uh, all right. Thanks for uh thanks for sticking with us tonight. Um, you know, exciting night for us. Um, we're excited. We very excited to add Jeremiah. Um, you know, happened happened quick there. We had to wait for two picks and uh we're excited to to call him and and let him know that he'd be joining us. Just um excited about the player, excited about the person, um you know, excited about what he's going to add to our team. So, um with that, I'll shoot it to you guys. He said you guys had a conversation last week and it went really well that you know it was just you guys hit it off right away. What was it about the dynamic that you think worked so well and >> I mean he's he's I mean you guys will get a chance to meet him tomorrow. Um he's just an impressive kid. Uh mature. Um has his head on his shoulders never gets too high, never gets too low. Um you know we had a great interaction with him at the combine. um you know, I followed up with him with a uh with a call over the weekend and um yeah, just had a had a great overall interaction. So, you know, like I said, you guys will get a chance to meet him. Impressive kid. Um you know, just really excited to add the person to our locker room. >> We don't know a ton about your offense yet, but what his how does he fit? How does his skill set fit into what you envision yourself doing? Yeah, I mean like I I've said this with running backs, you know, um they do come in all shapes and sizes. What's what's unique about him in my opinion is in all three phases. And what I mean by all three phases, the run game, the pass game, and protection, you know, he's he has the ability to to, you know, mix it in in all those, you know. So, you guys see all the explosive stuff. I mean, that that's all there, you know, but uh you know, he didn't have that weakness in my opinion in any of those phases. So, you can put him in those situations. You know, he's got to learn this game. He's got to learn the NFL. He's got to learn the speed of it. I mean, there's a lot still that that uh needs to be uh learned in practice and all that, but uh he definitely has the tools to get there. >> Monte, obviously uh when you're picking that high in the draft, there's a lot of conversation about premium positions and running back. How did you measure that or was it just a question of Jeremiah being that much better than everybody else? >> Yeah, I think Darren with that, you know, we're we're evaluating each each player, each position. We're stacking our board. Um, you know, when we're picking that high, the the goal is to add an impact player and um, you know, there were there were certainly other players that we talked about. Um, you know, we did we talked about the position. Uh, understand all that. In the end, we we felt we added the guy that could impact our team the most. Um, and just really excited about the versatility that he brings to the offense. it it's obviously generally easier and and cheaper to find running backs through other means, especially free agency, than it is offensive tackles and rushers. I guess like how much did that play into your thinking and and what made you willing to overlook um kind of that element of of um I guess scarcity at different positions? Um, I mean really tail, I mean I think with every decision that we make, we uh in the draft we take the best player that we think is available when we pick and we did that tonight. That'll always be the case. Um, and that's that will always be the case as as long as I'm here. I know that's what Mike believes in. It's what I believe in and that's what we did. >> How do you see the running back room sorting itself out being a little bit crowded now? >> Yeah, it is. It's a it's a good room. There's no question. and it's a good room and I think with with as with anything else the the competition will take care of itself. Um you know so that'll be for Mike and his staff to to sort out but you know it's a it's a good problem to have. >> The two picks ahead of you kind of went a little bit quick just in terms of the clock getting down. You guys obviously kind of went down to the final minute. Could you just talk through maybe the the trade conversations that you had? Did you guys come close to moving out of the pick? Like how did those go? >> Yeah, Donnie you want if you want me to tell you the honest god truth. we had the wrong phone number to uh the the the phone number that we were given was the wrong one and so that was a little bit of the delay. So we got that straightened out and we called Jeremiah and we got a hold of him. That's that's what the delay was. Um >> there was no delay. >> There was no delay. Yeah. Um technical difficulties. Um you know there was a very minimal conversations Donnie. There was you know some surface level but but nothing that came anywhere close to to getting us to move off the pick. Did you have any conversations about moving back into the first round 34 there? >> Yeah, we did. We did late in the draft. Um, you know, we kicked it around. Um, you know, I think I told you guys the other day, you start um you start counting the number of players that you would pick. Um, you know, and you look at it and you look at there was a number of teams that were looking, you guys saw there was a lot of movement there at the end of the first round. Um, so yeah, we had we had some conversations. Um, but, you know, it just didn't work out for us to move up. So, you know, tomorrow, uh, I think San Francisco ended up at pick 33, so, you know, they'll pick and then we're there at 34. >> Jeremiah Jeremiah said, um, that you guys were very authentic with him, very kind-hearted. Just did you get that same feel with him just immediately talking to him? >> He's just a real dude. He's a very, uh, easy guy to talk to. He's very mature. Um, like he said, he's got his head on on straight, you know, and he's about the right stuff. um comes from a great family. I think his story is awesome. Uh but but above all, right right like it's just like right when he walked in, you knew you had a man in there, you know, and uh he loves it. He's smart. He's tough. He's got all those those attributes, but uh he's going to be a good teammate for these guys. >> Obviously, when you're picking at three, there's not a ton of scenarios, right? So, at what point in the process did you kind of land on the idea that Jeremiah would would very likely be your guy at three? Yeah, I mean I think I think we came to a pretty solid conclusion of what where we were going, what we were doing at the start of this week. >> What did uh Jeremiah's father tell you about the guy you were considering drafting? I already had some nice things to say to both of you. >> Uh yeah, I don't know that. Yeah, I'm not sure we either of us spoke to his father. So >> absolutely. >> Yeah. Lonnie, with uh obviously you're you're looking at scenarios, but but there was a lot of time between after your pick and kind of watching how everything plays out. As you're going through that, are you guys just honed in on the round itself? Are you guys already starting to kind of look ahead and see what might be there in second round, etc., etc.? >> Yeah, I mean, I think I think, you know, there was a long time to wait there, Darren. And I think um you know there was 15 16 picks and and you know you just kind of sit there and wait. Um you know I think we had a uh we had a pretty good idea of what might make it till the end of the first round and who what guys we might be considering and then you know we tried to in our mock draft exercises we tried to uh go all the way out to 34 and and see what might be left. Um but really until it until it got to a point I mean call it 23 24 25 um you know really didn't have any discussions about you know you're just you're forced to wait and see what's left there. So that happened around I'd say pick 24 25 and then but nothing came of it and so we'll be we'll we sat where we're at. We'll see what happens tomorrow night. You guys talked last week about taking players based off not only where they are, but maybe where they can be in terms of becoming like an NFL player. A lot of times like top five picks are expected to be these franchise defining guys and game changers and stuff like that. And he's still a rookie obviously, but like where do you guys think Jeremiah can be as an NFL player? >> I think he can be I think he can help us in multiple ways. Mike mentioned um as a runner, as a receiver, in pass protection. Um, but you know, really like at this point his his job is to come in here, uh, meet his teammates, learn the system, um, you know, meet his coaches, uh, figure out just how we run things here and and really that's our expectation for for him right now. >> How many mocks do you guys run through and how accurate are they done with the first? >> Um, yeah, it's a great question. Um, we do we do an exercise on every year on I think we've done it on Monday or Tuesday. um where we we utilize our pro scouts. Um those pro scouts during the season, they have uh seven or eight teams that they're they're involved with. Um and then we just go through the draft and they they pick players according to um you know, media reports. They pick players based on what they know of the draft. Um, and we just we go through and then there's there's scenarios where we'll we'll do one, hey, do this one, you know, straight straight down the fairway and then we do another one. Hey, get a little wild with this one cuz I mean, as we saw tonight, there's things that maybe we didn't anticipate happening. So, that's the truth with every draft. And, you know, we we never get it 100% right, but it's it's a fun exercise to do and and to just see what might be there. with this decision-making process. Was ownership involved in this process in this decision at all? >> Uh in the decision? No. No, not at all. Um you know, Michael um Michael is involved to the point of uh he likes to know what's going on. He loves to hear about our process. He loves to hear about um how we have arrived at um at the board where it's at. Um you know, he's he's great at throwing us scenario. Well, what if this guy goes, "Okay, well then we would do this." So, uh, Michael's been great. He was awesome with letting Mike and I go through our process. Um, and he was he was engaged as always, but really hands off and let us do our job. >> Uh, with Jacobe reportedly asking for the raise, how might that impact everything moving forward through the draft and where do you guys currently stand with him? >> Yeah, had have had good dialogue. Both Mike and I have have had good dialogue with Jacobe. Um, obviously this is the voluntary portion of everything. Um, you know, we'll continue to have conversations with Jacobe, but you know, things are things are in a good spot. >> Mike, what are your initial thoughts when you add a guy with love's talent level to compliment um Marv, Michael, Trey? >> Yeah, just another piece of the puzzle like you just said. I mean, he's got, you know, there's like I'm not going to sit here and say we don't all see the skill set, obviously, but to add that skill set to what I already believe is a pretty good skill set with our receiver room, with our tight end room, to add to that running back room. Um, it's it's cool, you know, and again, like like Monty said, like the expectation is for him to come in here, learn the system, learn his teammates, and get right to work just like we're asking all these other guys to do, even the guys that have, you know, um, done something in this league. So, uh, I think he's going to fit in really well with these guys. But I know he's going to fit in really well with these guys because again he's he loves this and and all teammates want is guys that are going to come in and help him win and compete and fight hard and play tough and do all the things that it takes to move the needle forward. >> How different is the prep moving from round one to rounds two and three going into the market? >> Uh you know really not different at all, Donnie. There's just fewer names left up on, you know, there's 32 less names on the board. Um you know, so we'll u we'll regroup in the morning. um you know, we already have an idea of the the top two or three guys that that are on the board that that we know one of them is going to be there because there's only one pick in front of us the second. Um and then really it's the same, you know, we'll pick there early in the second or you know, obviously we'll always listen if there's any opportunities to move around. Um and then we got to wait for 32 more names to come off the board before it's our turn again. So, um really not different at all. There's just, you know, fewer and fewer names on the board as we go. >> How many picks surprised you today? >> Say again. >> How many picks surprised you today? Oh man, I don't know. There. I mean, there's always a few. >> Yeah, >> there was a few. There was a few, but I mean, it always happens, you know, like 32 different teams, 32 different boards. Like, you know, everybody um everybody sees them a little bit differently. >> Which one surprised you? >> Okay. >> None of them. His mock hit. >> 32. 32 out of 32. >> He won. He won first round bingo. Yeah. Yeah. >> You guys should do that. It's a good game. First round bingo. You write 32 names on the board. First first person that crossed off all 32 wins for entertainment purposes only. Of course, you know. >> Absolutely. >> Yeah. That's right. That'd be great. That'd be great. >> Friendly wagers. >> Yeah. >> Sorry. >> Yeah. I'll go for for Mike. Like how do you think a running back can elevate? like how can an elite running back elevate an offense and kind of change the dynamic of the stress you guys are putting under? >> Yeah, running back, receiver, tight end. Like there's no secret in this league, explosives are are are massive. When you look at, you know, um outside of obviously points, like what are the the two biggest factors statistically? It's turnovers and explosives. It's actually closer than you'd think. And so anytime any way you can generate explosive um that's a good thing for the offense. Anytime you can, you know, obviously li uh limit explosive from a defense, that's a good thing for the Arizona Cardinals, you know. So when you bring in explosive playmakers at any position, uh you're giving yourself a better chance to have those explosives. I don't got to call the greatest play. Sometimes when you just get the ball to a guy like Trey McBride, he breaks three tackles and he turns into explosive. You know, same thing with our receivers. And so anytime you can get that from the backs, it's just that next position that uh allows you to, like I just said, get those explosives. >> Awesome. See you guys tomorrow night. Yeah. Thank you guys. Thank you.

title: Instant Reaction: Bills Trade Out Of First Round, 9 Picks Heading Into Day Two
text: The Bills are pretty happy with what's left on their draft board. So, they get right out of the first round and they're sticking with the top of the second round. The Bills moved on three times to land at number 35. That's the third overall pick in the second round. Welcome into our NFL draft special. He's voice of the Bills, Chris Brown. I'm Mattie Glab. We heard a lot of people talk about the Bills possibly moving out of round one. Why was night one ripe for the Bills to move out? Yeah, I think we knew all along, Maddie, that this was a distinct possibility. Not only because of the lack of consensus in the bottom half of round one in terms of players that they deemed to be true firstrounders, so to speak, and I don't think they were alone. We saw six of the last seven picks get traded at the end of round one. I think that's an indication of the lack of consensus, and the Bills were part of that lack of consensus. And I think also the meat and potatoes of this draft, as we have said all along, is between rounds two and four and knowing the Bills didn't have a pick in round two, having given up pick 60 in the DJ Moore trade, I think Brandon Bean was bound and determined to find a way to recoup draft capital on day two. And he does that with these three trades that ultimately move him down a total of only nine spots from 26 to 35. So, in the grand scheme of things, you only slid back nine positions. And clearly, they have a cluster of players on their board somewhere between the end of round one and the first half of round two cuz you wouldn't be moving back nine spots unless you felt you were going to get players that were in that range on your board. They clearly have a lot of them in that area. >> So, kudos to Bill's general manager, Brandon Bean, for doing work in the first round and picking up a lot of draft capital. The Bills started out the night with just seven draft picks. They now have nine overall. Where does this help Buffalo the most? >> Well, I mean, I think it it helps in terms of where the best value on this draft board is. Rounds one through seven. The best value is considered to be between rounds two and four. They went from one day two day two pick to two. >> And they went from five day three picks to seven. And five of those seven picks they now have on day three are in rounds at four and five. I think more importantly, they're also picking in the top five. Yes. >> In the round in rounds two, round three, round four, and round six. They're picking third in round two, second in round three, first in round four, first in round six. They're also picking fourth in round seven for goodness sake. So, this is a team that is routinely picking at the bottom of the rounds because of how well they've done in the playoffs. Now they're in the top five in a lot of these rounds on day two and day three. I think Brandon Bean has done maybe one of his best jobs at positioning himself and the team in day two and three of the draft. >> Positioning positioning yourself in day two and day three of the draft knowing that's where the meat and potatoes exist. Having three different fourth round picks. Now you got your second round pick as well. When you relate that to the new coaching staff in this building, to the new defensive coordinator in Jim Leonard trying to put together a new three four defense, how is it helpful to have more darts to throw at the dart board? >> Well, not only do you have more darts, but let's look at how round one unfolded tonight, Maddie, because offensive tackles and guards dominated round one. There were seven offensive tackles and two guards. Nine offensive linemen came off the board. Um, only five edge rushers came off the board. I I don't think anybody would have guessed that. I think they would have largely expected it to be pretty even there. Nine O linemen and maybe eight or nine edge rushers. Only five come off the board. That's an advantage for Buffalo who, as we know, need edge rusher help. Only five receivers came off the board in round one. If the Bills are still mining for one in round three, maybe round four, there might still be some pretty good ones left on the board. And I think this is the most important thing, Maddie, and I think it's why Brandon Bean felt comfortable moving out of the round completely. We know they need linebacker help. We know they need defensive tackle help. We know they need safety help and maybe even a cornerback for depth. One off-the-ball linebacker came off the board, Sunny Styles. Two corners came off the board. Two defensive tackles came off the board and only two safeties came off the board. You have the third pick in round two. You could get one of the top three linebackers in the draft. You could get one of the top five corners in the draft. You can get one of the top five defensive tackles in the draft. You could get one of the top five safeties in the draft. The options are tantalizing when you're picking third on day two. >> Sitting at 26 and 91 to start this night. We knew Buffalo would have a long wait after their first round pick to then pick at the bottom of the third round. Now they're sitting at 35 and 66. You have way less time that you have to wait and you can take advantage of drafting some of those defensive positions if you believe this is what we need to make our roster better. And we know that we can find it on day two. >> Yeah. And and not only that, you've got three picks in round four, two picks in round five. I don't think Brandon Bean's done wheeling and dealing because now you can parlay those fourth round selections into maybe another third rounder because as we mentioned, you're round three. If you got somebody that's falling down the board in round three that you covet, you now have the wherewithal and the draft capital to make that move. You may get right back to where you were at 91. >> True. with some of the picks that you you have now in rounds four and five. So, I I just think that he Brandon Bean has positioned the team very well to not only get high value picks in rounds two through four, but he also now has the draft capital to move around the board as he and his personnel department see fit. Having more draft capital to do what you want in this draft is such a big advantage for Buffalo with the new coaching staff coming in here to start the 2026 season. It's interesting that we saw so many trades happen in night one because the weeks leading up to the draft, the consensus was the bottom of the first round is not as valuable as the top of the second round will be. So, it might be hard for teams to find a trade partner to get out of the first round. >> They ended night one with trade, trade, trade, trade, basically. >> Yeah. Six of the last seven picks got traded. >> Are you surprised by that? >> Well, I I think lack of consensus can be deemed to be one of two things. I think you can play both sides of the fence there. You can argue to your to your point what a lot of the analysts were saying that oh it might be hard to find a trade partner cuz there aren't a lot of first round grades on players. There's not a lot of consensus as to whether there are enough first round grades on players. But I think you could go the other way too because when there isn't that consensus that also means there are teams that really like players that maybe other teams don't like cuz they don't fit a system or they're only fit for this team. All you need is one team that really likes a player and wants to go up and get that player. And we kind of saw that at the end of round one. Like Chris Johnson, the corner, like Miami uh moved up from 30 to make sure they got him. They desperately needed a corner. I mean, Gerard M Jam McCoy, who was widely considered the second best corner in the draft and tested well off his knee injury in his proday, is still sitting on the board right now. He didn't even come off the board. So, it's different strokes for different folks. they wanted a bigger, taller corner, they go with Chris Johnson. Um, you there's several other examples here. Houston trades up with Buffalo two spots to get a guard and Keelin Rutled is going to be a really good player in this league, but they traded up two spots to get a guard. So, I think that speaks to just the uncertainty of who likes what and what might be one man's treasure is another team's trash. And that might be a strong statement, not trash, but you know what I'm saying to go back and forth. I think there's going to be a lot and I think this is going to continue. I think this is going to continue tomorrow in round two and I really think there's going to be a run on linebackers, defensive tackles, and safeties. Emanuel McNeel Warren was a player that a lot of people projected as a first round pick. He's still on the board. You've got Cashes Howell, the short armed pass rusher, you know, from Texas A&M. He's still on the board. Jacob Rodriguez, one of the best linebackers. CJ Allen, one of the best line Jake Gold, Anthony Hill, these are four of the top five linebackers. They're still sitting there. There's going to be a run on them and the Bills have positioned themselves to be part of that run no matter what position it is because they're picking third on day >> Speaking about picking on day two, the Bills have two picks right now, 35 and 66. What's available for them at 35, Chris? >> Yeah, I the linebackers that I just mentioned, I think if they want to get one of the best safeties in the draft, there's a chance one of them are available there at the top of round two. you can get your edge rusher there if there's somebody that fits the value whether it's Cashes Howell Armason Thomas I mean these are guys that are still sitting there on the board for you to pick from those linebackers I mentioned and that defensive tackle Christian Miller who some people had I mean we've had people on our daily show one bills live there are some people of the opinion that Christian Miller was the second best defensive tackle in the draft well Peter Woods went off the board and he was he and Caleb Banks at 18 and at 29 to Kansas City. So, you've got Christian Miller on the board and other defensive tackles that I think are going to merit consideration there, you know, uh whether it's Lee Hunter, the Texas Tech kid. So, I think it's going to be very heavy on defense here to start the second round. And as we said, the Bills have put themselves in an enviable enviable position at 35 to really get a quality player while acrewing all this extra draft capital that they can use now because now they're picking at the top of round three as well at pick 66. When looking at what Buffalo has when it comes to day two of the NFL draft, you mention all these names that could be available for the Bills, whether it's in the second round or the third round, based on players you've watched. Do you have any favorites available for Buffalo and who are those? >> I would be I mean, look, I think we all know by now I'm a little partial to Georgia, but I I really like CJ Allen and Christian Miller. I think those could be impact players right away for them. and I think they would merit consideration at pick 35. So, I'd be happy with either of those players, even if you got the safety, McNeel Warren. I mean, that's a that's a dynamic player for your defense. There are some who believe that CJ Gardner Johnson is going to be more of a nickel, okay, >> than a safety. And if that's their plan, >> then I think safety becomes a more prominent option and possibility. Round three, um, you're picking at 66 now. You're that's the second pick in round three. I absolutely love Trayen Stokes, the Arizona do everything defensive back. He's played outside corner. He's played safety. He's played nickel corner. I know he's 25 years old, but that's a guy that's ready to play for you right now. Had some of the most unbelievable tape I've ever seen for a defensive back in a long time. I'd be happy with him. Keonte Scott, the Miami uh do everything DB is another guy you could consider there. And if you don't take a defensive tackle in round two, you got Big Citrus there sitting in round three, Dominique Orange from Iowa State. These are the options the Bills have now given themselves with all this extra capital on day two and day three. >> It was interesting to see that second run on edge rusher happen. Now, it wasn't a big run. You saw three edge rushers go off the board. Ake Mezador was at 22 to the Chargers. Then you saw Malachi Lawrence from UCF go to the Cowboys. And then later to basically end the first round at 31, Kendrick Faulk from Auburn goes to the Titans. >> There's some edge rushers available for Buffalo if they decide that's the direction we want to go in. That was a favorite position being mocked to Buffalo in the first round. You still have talent available at the top of the third round. One player who was a favorite name for Buffalo for mock drafts was edge rusher Cashes Howell out of Texas A&M. 11 and a half sacks last season. He's got great bend, a really quick first step, is powerful, and kind of is a dominator out there. >> Yeah, SEC defensive player of the year, too, if I remember right. And you also have Arm Mason Thomas, who's a player that I like a lot, too. Um, I don't know if he is a consideration at 35, but if you trade back again because you like everything that's sitting on the board, maybe he comes into play if you're sitting at 40 or 41 and you go with R. Mason Thomas, who I think is a very complete edge rusher because not only can he rush the passer very effectively, he's really good on the edge, supporting the run and setting the edge out there, which is saying something for a 241 pound player. Not all of these top edge rushers are good against the run. I believe Armason Thomas is in my estimation, one of the more complete uh edge rushers in the class. You got Gabe Jacis who could be a consideration if you slide down in round two a little bit later in the round. And we haven't really talked about receiver, but I think in round three there could be some intriguing options on the board at receiver. Whether you're talking about Malachi Fields from Notre Dame, um Antonio Williams from Clemson, Deshawn Stribbling has moved up boards, the Old Miss kid with a lot of elite physical traits. So I think there's options at receiver in round three as well. The Bills, look, I know some people just want the high prized possession in round one, but the Bills are picking a 26. They saw a lot of value on their board. Slide back nine spots, add two picks, get a lot of draft capital to work with on day two and day three. I really feel like they've put themselves in a very advantageous position to really help their roster. >> And look, there were several players still available that were projected to go on night one by plenty of NFL draft analysts. So, it's not that they get out of round one and there's no round one talent available. there's still some talent available that they could have graded as round one talent and figure they're still available so we're going to get out of the first round and we're going to pick them up in the second round and pick up some more picks while we're at it as you think about how night one happened all the trades. What was the biggest surprise in your eyes? >> It's probably Tai Simpson right to the Rams at 13. Um, if you told me that the Rams took a quarterback in round one, I don't know that I'd be stunned because we know that, you know, Matthew Stafford's 38 and while he's still great, you know, and was MVP, he's probably got two years left, like two really good years left, um, to make hay with the Rams. And so finding a quarterback of the future made sense. I thought they might have slid back lower in the round and then he's a consideration at 20 or maybe 21. Um 13 seemed a bit rich for me. I thought they could have moved back and still gotten him. And I think that's what made it such a surprise for me. Not that they picked a quarterback, but where they picked him. 13 for a one-year starter with 13 career starts. That's a big swing. A big swing for a quarterback. And I know he played in a similar system there at Alabama that he will play for the Rams. And so maybe that's what made them feel more comfortable about him being an answer for them. But but that was an awfully big swing for them. >> One thing that caught my eye from the first round is the Jets getting three first round picks. David Bailey, Kenyan Sadi, Omar Cooper Jr., Aaron Glenn, and company with the Jets, they're ready to have a hall and show the AFC East we want to we want to be competitive this year. >> Yeah. I mean, playmaker Kenyan Sadi absolutely. Omar Cooper Jr. I mean, they're trying to help Gino Smith as much as they can. And then they got the pass rusher, David Bailey, obviously at the top of the draft. You know, in Miami, uh, you know, moved around a little bit, too. They get an offensive tackle in Kaden Proctor. So, you know, that was a good move for them. And they get a quarterback, which they sorely needed in Chris Johnson later on in the round with a move up the board with San Francisco. So, you know, they did some things there. And then even New England gets into the first round or further up the board in the first round in a trade with Buffalo and take an offensive tackle in Caleb Lomu. I think there's a very good chance that their offensive tackle that started last year as a rookie in Campbell might move inside to guard and it might be this kid Lomu starting at left tackle. So they might have a rookie at left tackle for the second year in a row. And we didn't really think about this Maddie. This is the second time in three years that the Bills move out of round one. >> True. >> They did it in the Keon Coleman draft. >> Yeah. It's something that I think a lot of people had their their radar on radar on about it is Buffalo possibly moving out of that first round just with how people explained this draft class and where the meat and potatoes of this draft class was. And the Bills do it and they pick up more picks while they're at it. I think it's really going to help out the Bills and their product on the field. The only other surprise pick I saw in round one was Caleb Banks at 18 to Minnesota. >> That was a little surprising. >> Felt like a little bit of a reach. Plus with the with the surgery concerns with his foot, he's had three procedures on that same foot in 18 months. He's supposed to be ready for training camp after getting another procedure done just in March after the combine found some irregularities in there. So, that's a big risk to take at pick 18 when you had the pick of the litter at defensive tackle. I mean, he's an intriguing prospect that's 66, 325, but health concerns, I don't know if I would have made that pick at 18. That seemed a little rich for me. >> It'll be interesting to see how healthy he is for his rookie season. We also saw two running backs go. Everybody was saying one running back is going to be Jeremiah Love, and you see two from Notre Dame go. The Seahawks stick and pick at number 32 to get their running back because their guy, their Super Bowl MVP, no longer with the team now Kansas City Chiefs. >> Yeah. And the Chiefs made a nice big move up the board too uh earlier in the night. Um or did they slide back? >> They traded up to number six and they got >> Monsour Delane. >> Yeah. So, they're always doing something. They leaprogged Washington because I think they knew that if Delane was still on the board for Washington, he would have gone seventh overall. So, they jumped ahead of them and took him at pick number six in a trade with Cleveland. >> The Bills decide to move back in the first round and then they just kept moving and moving until they were completely out of night one. They're happy with what's available and they're going to pick near the top of round two. Started the night out with seven picks, end out with nine. General manager Brandon Bean has Bean has got to be happy as he's walking out the door tonight because he knows he's got more draft capital to work with on days two and three. That's going to do it for us. We appreciate you tuning in to our NFL draft special. And don't forget to tune in to days two and three of the NFL draft on NFL Network ESPN and ABC. Day two begins at 700 p. p.m. We'll see you then.

title: EXCLUSIVE: 1-on-1 Interview with first round pick Monroe Freeling | NFL Draft | Carolina Panthers
text: I'm here with the newest Carolina Panther Monroe Freeling first round pick out of the University of Georgia. For starters, you hear your name called, describe [clears throat] that moment. I mean the phone call was kind of funny. I I think I said I love you. I did not I wasn't thinking I feel like I was so surreal and I actually ran out of tears. I was just talking to me about it, but yeah, hear my name called especially just in my home state almost it's like it was surreal. I mean it was awesome. Like just thinking like wow like I'm not picking up and going across the country. I'm just going down the road. So it was awesome. When you have a moment like that often you kind of go back in time and you think of what got you to that point. What was the first moment that you thought of as a flashback? I mean really just the fact that like I was playing how for how long I've been playing football and everything that took and especially like this last year I felt like was so like tough especially coming off of such a tough game. I went to lay him surgery and then I was just kind of out and the whole spring and I didn't really get to do much and so the fact that I came all this way and and I'm at this point I'm now I'm a professional football player as what I wanted to be as a young and was it's just insane. It really is surreal. Charleston area kid. What connection if any did you have to the Carolina Panthers growing up? You know I didn't I don't really have any allegiance cuz I ended up I moved there when I was like 10 years old or not 10 but 12 or something. But there was a lot of you know Carolina fans around me and you know funny thing is that I think that a lot of the fan bases especially Clemson and South Carolina were mad at me for going out of state. So I hope I can repay them now that I'm here. They love me now. They love me now. >> here in Carolina. So yeah, no it's really good thing but I didn't really have true allegiance to any team especially as growing up. >> One of the things we've heard in the last 24 hours is what a great athlete you are. Where do you get the athleticism from mom or dad? My mom. Definitely my mom. My dad's not going to like to hear that but definitely my mom. What kind of athlete was mom? She played basketball, she played volleyball in high school and then she's kind of a triathlete and now she's done yoga for almost 10 years now and I get that from her too. Your dad does have an athletic past too. Tell us about that. Yeah, so he didn't play a single snap of American football but he played rugby whenever he was growing up and you know weird thing about dads is that you really don't get to hear a lot about their past until just some random night on a random Tuesday. So I don't know if I'm going to find out more about his past and how good he was at rugby but he played yeah that in South Africa. So Let's go back to mom and yoga because yoga's had an impact on your life growing up. How did you get introduced to yoga? Yeah, so my freshman year of high school was COVID happened which is crazy if you think about it but yeah COVID happened and there wasn't really much going on and so my mom was like hey you want to start doing yoga and we actually just got a weights in my garage. So I was really starting to like lift and like get bigger and so we just started doing yoga my mom was like you want to do yoga? So we invited some of the some of the other offensive lineman over that were on my team and we just started doing yoga in our garage and it kind of built from that and I started and there was so many like benefits to it like I wasn't as sore and I was you know able to lift more and there was just so many benefits that I noticed and I just kind of kept it going and here I am now and it's still with me and I think it's I credit it to a lot of my athleticism I think. Is the breathing aspect something that you've used as well whether it's in a big moment that that breathiness they teach you? No definitely. I think that also like whenever I did get injured in 24 or 25 the whole off season I ended up starting meditating before games and so I don't know if that came with it but I do know that like there was sometimes I think I gave up a sack this last year against Tennessee and I was like now I'm just going to come back to my breath like that's what yoga's all about and you know being in those compromising positions especially like whenever you're tired or whatever but no it definitely makes a difference. You had a brother who played basketball at Queens right here in Charlotte. What has he told you about your new hometown or your new town? I mean he's going to have to tell me more but I came and visited him like a couple times I think but I mean for the most part I think he was kind of locked in on campus. I'll have to find out whatever he said and what he has to say about Charlotte but I mean I know it's a great city. I mean I'm it's again it's insane that I'm actually here. I'm really here in Charlotte. It feels like it was meant to be just my brother was here like the high school coaches here like everyone's here. So You go to Georgia and a lot's been made that you only started 18 games but I look at Georgia's defense and all the guys that they turned out that are playing in the NFL. What did that do for you in practice facing future pros every day? I mean it gave me confidence number one in my decision to come out which has paid off as we can see but really just the fact that I was be able to go against so many NFL guys made me a better football player and like people say only 18 starts but yeah I have like a thousand starts against these NFL players that are playing in the league right now. So it's like it's it definitely helped me with my career. What else was it about Georgia and playing in the SEC that you feel prepared you for the NFL? I mean I don't know if you've been to any of our practices but they're brutal. So from everyone's feedback from any NFL team from players that have left Georgia say it's 10 times easier. So that's definitely something that I like now I wouldn't say I'm looking forward to the practice being easier but definitely a little less on my body but also just like the attention to detail we have at Georgia I think is really been the culture we have. So coming to a place that has such a strong fan base and such a culture like I see the core traits they have all over the walls here. I'm really excited to come to a place that has such a strong culture cuz I think that is really what makes or breaks teams and especially the keep pounding go to the fourth quarter.
