He's not a selfarter. How do you respond to that? And what does your preparation look like now, now that you're in the NFL and you're playing with the Miami Dolphins? Yeah, I mean, yeah, it it definitely was. It was like that. You know, I was 400 lb, you know, when and Coach S was there, you know, in the offseason. Um, you know, that summer, my freshman year, but I feel like I've, you know, got a couple years under my belt to where I've I've kept that in check, you know, I've built and and put a plan in place to to go succeed and to to be at the weight that I need to be um to go out there and provide for the team. So, Michelle Hi, thanks and congratulations. Welcome to Miami. I'm just wondering uh I'm from the Miami Herald. What do you know about Miami and about the idea of living in Miami, the Miami lifestyle? Do you ever come here on vacation? What do you know about Miami? Thanks. >> I haven't been to Florida too too much. You know, I I've been down to Dest with my boys on spring break. But, um, the first time I was at Miami, well, Fort Lauderdale was for my 30 visit. And, you know, I love the city. Um, and I feel like it's it's going to be a good time. You know, have have a fun time down there. Um, but the biggest thing for me is, hey, man, no state taxes. That's a blessing right there. A blessing.

title: General Manager Jon-Eric Sullivan meets with the media | Miami Dolphins
text: Proctor and why you felt really good about him to to move back and take him over. >> Sure. Yeah, good question. Um, he's unique. He's rare. Uh, he's a 350lb man with unique athletic traits that can play four spots across the line of line of scrimmage, the left tackle, right tackle, both guards. Um, the athletic traits for a man his size are through the roof. You know, I know there's been some questions about his weight. It's well documented. Obviously, we were very aware. We did our due diligence uh with our resources. We feel really good about where he is at uh with that. And um we brought him in on a 30 visit. Uh I could feel his conviction and his desire to be a good football player and do the things that he needs to do to be the best pro that he can be. Um all I can tell you is that there wasn't another one in the draft like him. period. >> Do you envision him starting off at tackle? >> You know what I mean? That's I think I think I I don't want to pigeon hole him. We'll give them to the coaches and kind of we we'll get the best five out there. I do think he has the unique ability to play all four spots at a really high level. Um it's hard to say. You know, we got some other guys. Obviously, Brew is very, you know, he's a center so that's but you know, Pat Paul and then you had Jonah and Jo, you know, who knows? Uh and then and then Austin. We're excited about him coming back healthy at right tackle. So, we'll just do what we need to do to get the best five out there. Uh the unique thing about him is he can line up in all those spots and you feel really good about it. >> There's always going to be second guessing and wondering I think for people on the direction you go when you look at the situation where you had 11, you had Caleb DS potentially there or a guy like Ruben Bane, a local guy. How is that process in real time as it's happening or was it a situation where you were set on Proctor regardless at that point? >> You know what, uh the other, you know, Downs and Bane are marvelous players. Um, and I understand the question and I I think those guys will go on to be very successful in this league. No doubt about it. Again, we thought uh we thought Proctor was was rare. His height, weight, speed, production, the things that he can do uh on the football field for a man his size, he's an outlier. There's there's there's not many like him. Um that's it has, you know, it's no shot at. Caleb D's a phenomenal phenomenal football player and he'll have a great career and we would have loved to have him here, but we had a lot of conviction on on Proctor being a very unique player in this draft and one that uh that that we can build around for years. Um, you know, we invested in Malik and it was important for us to protect him to make sure that he has time to do the things that he needs to do uh and keep him healthy, you know, so that was part of the conversation as well. Um, so yeah, we uh we're thrilled with the pick. We're happy to add him. We have a lot of faith in the person. Um and and we think he's going to be a really good player here. You know, no apologies. >> You mentioned in the 30 visit that he was impressed at how straight you guys were. You said you guys were straight shooters. What expectations did you guys line out uh to him when you spoke with him? >> Yeah, it was more just a real honest direct conversation with substance. You know, we we we asked him to walk >> us through his time at Bama, the lessons he learned, the back and forth from Iowa, the weight. Um, and he didn't hide from any of it, you know, and he talked about his growth and the things that he learned through that journey. Um, and then obviously we have our resources at Bama who have been with him recently, you know, over the last couple years and, uh, and we have really good relationships there and, you know, things like competitive, prideful, uh, never wants to be embarrassed, leads the conditioning runs. Um, you know what I can tell you about him is, you know, I don't need to name name the coach by name, but there was a coach there at one point who was militant about weights. Um, he didn't worry about Proctor's weight. That wasn't an issue for him because he could handle it. Um, the guy's got 270 pounds of lean body mass. You know, he's just a naturally large human being. Um, but he's not a fat guy, you know, and if if you put your eyes on him when he gets around here, you'll see that pretty quickly. So, I say all to say, look, none of us have a crystal ball. You don't know what the future's going to bring. Uh, but we feel really good about what we invested in tonight as a as a human being, as a professional, and as a football player. >> So, you said last week that you guys run through simulations of how the draft could go. How many scenarios did Kaden fall to you guys at 11? Um, most to be honest with you, most we were good with that. Uh, now there were some teams that were trying to move up. You know, I'll keep those teams to myself, but there were some teams trying to move up and we felt pretty good, uh, at least about one of them, uh, coming to get him. So, um, you know, we're excited about how this night ended. Um, you know, it was an organizational decision. Our coaches loved him, our scouts loved him. All the analytics told you this guy's a unique, rare guy. Um, so I, you know, again, I can't, uh, I understand the questions and, you know, that's just the way this business goes. Like, whoever you pick, you know, you guys are going to have questions about why you didn't do this and why you didn't do that, and that's okay. You got a job to do. Understand that. Not mad at you for it. Um, but just know we feel really good about who we invested in tonight. Flipping to the other side of the ball, um what stood out to you about Chris Johnson and how did you evaluate, you know, the Mountain West play versus some of the other guys that play SEC, Big 10, etc., etc. >> Yeah, you know, when you watch Chris, he's got great feet, great balance and body control. He's physical. He's a big corner. He can play nickel, play outside corner. He's got ball skills. I mean, when you start checking the boxes for a defensive back, there wasn't really left. there were there weren't really many left. Uh there were none really. He'll tackle, you know, he's again physical. Um he's just got and he's got upside. He's 21 years old. He's a good kid. He handles his business. He works. He wants to be a good player. Um he's about the right stuff. He's the kind of guy that we want to infuse into this uh into this locker room as is Proctor. You know, those guys are football's important to them and uh and they both have edge. You know, they have edge to them. Uh they both in a good way reek of confidence, not arrogance, but confidence. You know, they think they're players and all those things were important to us as we build this thing out. >> For a second, you you said that most scenarios he was going to fall to you. What did you guys value in him then that other team might not have? What you see that you said he's going to work here? >> You want me to go through it again? >> No, no, no. But you said most most scenarios had him fallen to you. Sure. >> And two two tackles were taken right before you. >> Yeah. >> Um why what did you guys value that? >> Why do you think you valued them and other teams didn't? >> I don't think that other teams didn't value him. Like I said, I know one team in particular was trying to come up to our spot to get them. Um and there there was another that was calling and I have a pretty good, you know, pretty good sense that they were too. You I can't speak for the other 31 teams. I wouldn't even pretend to do that uh to be able to do that. But, you know, again, the things that we valued were the size, the athleticism, the ability to play bully ball. You know, all the things I stated. You know, you can't play through him. He's hard to play around. He could play four spots. He's versatile. Um, we just felt like he was a a unique player. >> You stayed at 11. Would it still have been Proctor or was would Downs have been the guy? >> Proctor. >> Yeah. So, you said last week you'd rather have two good players than one special one in terms of whether you wanted to trade up or down. What was it about Chris Johnson specifically that you said we need to trade up? >> I think it was the versatility and I think it was the upside. You know, we feel like he's really gifted. Uh he's young. Like I said, he's 21. We feel like, you know, he can play really uh, you know, he'll play nickel or he'll play corner, but we also feel like, you know, depending on how this thing goes over, he he'd go back there and play safety as well because of the ball skills and the instincts. I don't think we'd end up doing that. He's going to play a corner, play nickel. Um, but we just we had a lot of conviction on him. We got a lot of picks. We felt like we had the flexibility to do that because of some of the draft capital that we had. And we stayed whole, you know, we didn't we didn't we swapped. We didn't lose. you know, we started the day with 11, we got 11 now. So, felt like it was the right thing to do. >> You've gone over some of the individual qualities of the players that you selected. Um, in the bigger picture, can you talk about the trenches with with Proctor and getting a cornerback, which you needed, and and you know, starting off the defense uh with with a corner. >> Sure. I'm sorry. Just say that again. Um, talk about building the trenches, which you said is a priority with Proctor and then with with Chris Johnson, you know, you get a cornerback to to kind of build the secondary. >> Sure. >> Yeah. I mean, it just you follow the board, you know? I mean, you always want to you if you can help it, I think you always, at least the way I was taught in this thing, you want to build it from the inside out, but you're not going to reach on guys. You got to follow the board. And we felt like, you know, the way the board was sitting at the time when Chris was there, um, he was he was we felt for us he was the best player available. And and again, it's, you know, you guys know how this thing goes. It's it's subjective. You know, you do all the work in the that you can. You got your analytics, you got your coaches, you got your personnel staff. Um, and you do you do that for a reason. Uh, and when you have conviction on a on a player, organizational conviction, uh, I think you have to listen to that. That's why that's why you go through the process and and he was one that we had that kind of conviction on and uh and so we do what we did. >> You said the word conviction a a lot as this is your first war room with this team as the GM. What was that process like as the voices in there and and and getting to that point where you were all in alignment to make these couple of picks? Like what was that process like? >> Sure. Just a you know a lot of work by a lot of people as you well know. Um, and then a lot of conversations, you know, we we have, you know, we have multiple meetings, um, you know, throughout the month of April, throughout the month of March. Uh, we have February draft meetings, but we keep it all separate because we're trying to identify the outliers. That's the way we do it. I don't want group think. I'm I'm trying to eliminate bias, which can happen when you have everybody in the room doing it at one time. Um, these two guys, to be perfectly honest with you, we didn't have we never had there were no outliers. We were convicted on these guys. You know, the analytics did it here, coaches did it here, we did it here, and then we brought it together and we looked at it. We were aligned from the jump on these guys. We saw it the same. And I told you before, like, you know, I don't need the validation of alignment all the time, but it helps, you know, it helps for for a healthy organization. You know, at the end of the day, the buck stops with me. I take responsibility for every player we pick, whether it turns out the way you want it to or whether it goes south. uh it stops with me. I'm not hiding from it. I really like what we did tonight and uh you know it's the bottom line. >> In the case of Chris Johnson, how important was his performance at the combine toward either getting your eyes focused on him or solidifying what you already knew? No, >> it's a great question and be honest with you is very important. Uh somebody mentioned the conference he plays in, you know, you know what I mean? I think at the end of the day, you're always looking for traits, right? I told you guys before, at least in my mind, this this this game at this level is played by men with traits, you know, and he you watched him play in in the fall and he had all the he had the feet, he had the balance, he's instinctive, he has all those things, ball skills, but then you're like, "All right, I want to see how he measures up with those corners in the SEC and he ran real fast and he jumped real high and all of a sudden you're going, "All right, you got a 6 foot plus 193 pound corner nickel that can play three, four spots that ran ran fast, jumped high, broad, you know, all of it. And it just helps you come to a conclusion that, yeah, this guy's exactly what I think he is. Not only is the film really good, not only is the upside really good, but all the traits in the world that uh that that you could want in a in a in a guy who has to cover players at this level, he's got them. He's got recovery speed. Uh he's got short area quickness. Um all those things, you know, it shows itself on tape, but then he validated it at the combine, which gives you peace of mind. trades with both picks. Uh what was all the wheelie and wheeling uh high level of activity like for you and what do you think of what you got out of those trades aside from the players? >> Yeah, I mean I think the fact that you know I've already shared with you how we felt about Proctor and he was kind of our guy. Um, so yeah, to come out it with with with two extra picks and not really, you know, just free money, you know. Um, so, you know, feel really good about it, you know, and then to go up and get a guy in Chris that we had a lot of conviction on and not lose a pick, you know, still stay whole. Feel good >> So, what was >> last week? You were up here and you mentioned that you had a dream. You woke up to a couple names off the board. Uh curious if either of these two players were one of those guys. >> You know what? I I'll keep the names to myself that they weren't and and I you know for full transparency I think I must have been back in Green Bay because I was actually pulling a tag off the board and we have digital here. Everything's digital. So uh but uh um no it wasn't one of the two. But uh I think it just tells you about the excitement you know that that I had that we had. Uh, we've been talking about this day, spent a lot of time in the draft room, hours upon hours trying to get to this point and prepare. And, uh, you know, we're excited. We feel like it was a really good first day. But, uh, it's, uh, it was, it was a funny dream. I was pulling the tag and I I literally woke up and I thought to myself like, damn, I was in Green Bay. It wasn't digital. >> Almost kind of building off of that question, what was this day like for you leading up to the start of the first round? You know, first do you have a post note in your pocket said Kaden Proctor no matter what or >> No, you know, you you have all that time on the front end of the day. You know, it's like the day itself takes a month, you know, to finally get to 8:00. But, uh, for me, I just I think sometimes you just go back to the simplicity of everything. You know, you read through your notes, you look at the great you look, how do I feel about him? How do our coaches feel about him? How do our scouts that do a great job feel about them? and you know, you start weighing things out and and it it speaks to you. It talks to you. And look, man, there's there's a lot of other really good players that were on the board um that are still on the board. Uh but that's this business. You got to make decisions. Um and uh feel good about the ones we made today. >> For the record, just asking like your nerves, the calmness of it, like what went through your brain as you're preparing for this? Yeah, it was I mean I I came in, we met with our guys, uh I got a workout in which helped me kind of clear my head and then uh I mean and this is this is just the truth of it. There there was an eerie calm for me like it's the work is done like this is the fun part. Now that doesn't mean you know things can heat up and go you know in moments when trades are happening things get going fast but you stay calm and you communicate and you and you you know you do what you need to do for your team. It's the execution piece of it. The work is in and has been done and it's like there there was a calm that came with the preparation. Uh which was I didn't expect it. It was pretty cool to be honest with you. I kind of I told somebody beforehand like I you know there's a like I feel like I should be more anxious. I'm not. I trust the people in the room. I trust our work. I trust the process. And uh like I said, I think the Dolphins got better today. I'm reading a quote here from the athletics uh scouting guide from a NFL scout who said that Chris Johnson's give a damn factor to the moon. Leader of the DB room, likable kid. His parents did an amazing job. I was just curious to get your perspective on your guys' background with Chris Johnson. >> Yeah, everything you just said, you know, we did a lot of work on him like we do on all the players. Um the coaches San Diego State couldn't have said better things about him. His care factor is high. He was a captain, team captain there. He's a leader. Uh he works. Um the intangibles along with the athletic traits along with the fact that he's a good football player lead to the conviction why we did what we did. You know that's uh you know I I told you guys from the jump you know um it's important that we we had the right kind of people here and Proctor's in that I mean you know he didn't hide from it and he's we feel like he's going this way and so do the people who've been around him you know over the last couple years. Um, these these are young people. Young people make mistakes. They have bumps in the roads. If I peel the layers back on all you guys when you were young, I know I made my mistakes. I'm sure y'all did, too. These kids aren't any different, you know? They're no different, you know, and they and they deserve, you can't bury them because they stubbed their toe along the way. I mean, there's certain things you won't forgive, but a guy who's, you know, battled his weight a little bit here and there and has gotten together and played really good football, you know, you got to give guys their due and see where they're going, not where they've been all the time in my opinion. >> I heard a coach say the other day that your first round pick or first round picks in your case are supposed to change the tone of practice. How do you I don't know if you I don't know if you subscribe to that, but how do you believe these two guys kind of change the the tone of practice? >> Sure. Um you know, I I think with Proctor when he walks out there, he's going to change the tone of practice. uh just with his size and his mass and I I think when when when you see people try to when they run into him and he you know the stopping power that he has, the ability to move uh large men coming off the ball in the run game um you know that'll speak for itself, you know. Um, and again, I I just I think the I think the raw athleticism of of of Johnson and again his ability to be versatile uh with his athletic traits and his mental, you know, smarts, you know, I think I think they'll recogn I think the team will recognize that pretty quick and respect it. You know, that's what I would say. >> So, as you look >> as you look to day two, is it still best player available or do you feel some needs? >> No, it's uh need comes into play. Hey, I mean, we'll always follow the board in terms of value, but you know, if you're looking at two guys that have the same value and and and you need one more, then it comes into play. That makes sense, you know. Um, got to, you know, yes, there there there do there does come a point where you're trying to fill holes, but you're not going to not follow the value of the board. >> There's obviously high expectations, you know, obviously based on what you said about Parker. How much do you have to help him understand and not this conversation from the outside get to his head and put even more pressure on him to perform? >> Yeah, you know, I mean, it's a good question. I think part part of it when you when you when you draft these guys, you have faith in our I have faith in our building and the people in this building. I have faith in Coach Hafley. I have faith in Coach Yenszer. have faith in, you know, our nutritionists and our strength staff and all the people that come to work here every day that are really good at their job. Um, you know, every I said this to our the first and I hate to use the word speech, but the first talk I gave to the building, like we all have a job to do and nobody here is more important than the other. Like we all have a role in this thing to get this place where we need it to get to. Um, and that's part of it. Like that's why you have a building full of people that have different jobs is to help these players be the best that they can be. And I have a lot of faith in this building and the people that come to work here every day. I also have faith in him that he's going to do the things that he needs to do. So um you know and he's been at Bama, you know what I mean? He's been at Bama and he's been out there every week playing uh you know he lined up every you know every Saturday and played good ball. You know go watch the tape. I mean it's that's you know I'll sit down and watch the tape with any of you if you want to. You tell me. >> Is that an opening business? >> Yeah, I was about to say >> at some point tomorrow. >> All right, y'all have a good night. See you. Take it easy.

title: Carnell Tate and Keldric Faulk on Joining the Titans | Press Conference
text: Go ahead, Mike. >> Well, welcome. Uh, certainly an exciting day here. Um, you know, what's better than having uh one first round pick than than having two. Um, so, you know, we couldn't be more excited to uh to to welcome Carnell Tate and Kendrick Faulk to to the Titans organization. Um, you know, just two obviously outstanding football players. They're even better human beings. Um they embody everything that we want uh in this organization. Uh their work ethic, resiliency, uh toughness, intelligence. Um they have it all and that's why they're sitting up here today. So uh without further ado, uh we'll open it up to questions here. >> Right. >> Go ahead, guys. >> Go ahead, TD. Uh going to start with Carnell. Uh since getting drafted, obviously it's been a busy whirlwind, but have you had a chance to do a little bit more homework to to learn about the team that you're joining and particularly the offense and the quarterback? >> Um yes, since being drafted, that's all I've been doing was just watching videos, all the guys here. Bunch of great group of guys that's here, great coaches, great uh players. So yeah, all I've been doing was just getting familiar with the players and the coaches. Terron Davenport, ESPN for you, Coach Salah. Obviously, the measurables are all there with with Kellrick and and what he brings to the table. How much are you banking on you and your coaching staff to be able to maximize the most out of him? Um, >> well, it's gonna be hard. Look at him. >> But, uh, no, we we, you know, knock on wood, we've we've had a lot of history with uh uh um guys with his skill set from Eric Armstead, guy, a gentleman who's here uh with us now with John Franklin Myers. Uh we drafted Mike Williams a year ago. Um we know exactly uh what to uh what's going to be great with him with his uh how to utilize his strengths, if you will. But uh sky's is the limit for this young man. He's young. Um there's a lot of football that he's got to learn, but we're excited to have him. >> Terry McCormack, main street media coach. This is also for you. Where do you see Kelch fitting in that front seven? What kind of how many different ways do you feel like you can use him? >> Yeah, we're we're um uh we're going to roll eight or nine on game day and uh we roll them pretty good. Um we try to keep our guys around 60% play time at max. Uh keep them fresh, keep them rolling. Um, we see him outside on early downs and pop him uh kick him inside on uh on pass downs and that's uh uh we think he's got an elite trait to rush a passer on the inside and uh combination between him, Jeffrey, u John Franklin Myers, I mean it's that it's a pretty lethal combination between the three of them and um we'll find different ways to get them all on the field. >> Robert Paul KuharskiPk.com um you guys have obviously brought in a lot of defensive talent now. now more on the line and you've talked about guys that could start outside and go inside and the 60% and all that. Could you talk in more detail? I mean, you've got a lot of guys that could start on the outside and pop inside, but only so many third downs to to to to do that on. How do you sort out the wide nine in particular? Who who's there right now in your head? And and even in that 60%, how do you sort out outside to inside when you have so many guys that fit that bill? >> No, for sure. That's one that's why Aaron Whitecon gets paid so much money. Um but um but no, in all seriousness, you know, you I I know the two obvious ones are Jacob Martin and uh uh Germaine, but I I think a lot of people are forgetting about Fei. Uh I think he you know, he was drafted last year. He's a talented young man. Um, you know, we're going to do our best to try to uh to give him every opportunity to be successful as a as a wide nine edge rusher on third down. And, uh, we feel really good about the rotation that's being built here. I think Borggo's done a great job collecting a group of men that have different skill sets and have versatility to them. And um look, when when you guys start watching us and uh you'll start seeing what we do third downwise with regards to our alignments and all the different fronts that we'll create to try to create one-on- ones and mismatches and um you know, so with regards to the complexity of it, it it is complex uh trying to get all these guys on the field, but uh it's something that we're very comfortable with, something that we've done in our past and something we'll continue to do. >> Jim Wyatt from Tennessee.com. I guess this is both for Carnell and Kellendrick. What have the last 24 hours been like for both of you guys and what's it been like kind of going through this process together? >> Uh the last 24 hours uh they kind they kind of been a little hectic. Uh mostly exciting though just because uh I get to start a new part of my journey. So um yeah it just really been exciting. uh came in the building today to get to know uh some of the great people in this building and um you know I brought my family down here so uh they get to witness it as well. So it's been great. Yeah. >> Yeah. Like like Kendrick said it's been hectic uh the past 24 hours. I mean this is all we ever worked for. Uh we're very appreciative of the Tit Titans organization for believing in us and then they also wouldn't be for without our parents and our family that got us this far. So, we appreciate them all and we appreciate the Titans organization for bringing us in. >> Uh, this question is for Carnell. Uh, it's Courtland Griffin three-point conversion. Uh, Carell, your time at Ohio State, you played a myriad of roles. You played outside, inside, XZ slot. How do you feel like that's prepared you for your role here in Nashville? Uh, and then how fun is it going to be for you to learn from a guy like Greg Lewis who will be your wide receivers's coach, and then Calvin Ridley, who will be your WY veteran? um playing different roles on the offense has just allowed me to thrive and also just allow me to understand the concepts that way if any guy goes down I can I can move and go to different positions. So that just shows how versatile you I am. And then also like with these guys up here if they put me in a position to go in the slot I'm ready for it. I've seen that look. >> Uh Junior Cooper WSMV4 this is for Carnell. You got to meet Cam today in person. I mean what was that interaction like and what stood out the most about him? Uh it was a fun interaction. Uh Cam's a great guy, elite talent, elite quarterback. Um great guy. Um I I grew up watching him. I watched him at Washington State. U so you just we can't get out wait to get out there and light it up together. >> Mike Paddton uh with uh touring the AFC South. I want to ask both of you, have you had a chance to check out just the offenses that offense and defense that you're both joining? And what's the immediate things that stood out to you as to where you would fit in and what you can be able to contribute? >> Um, yeah. So, I actually got I just got done watching a few plays uh today. Um, whatever the coaches need me to uh go out there and play, that's why I think I fit in. Whatever they ask for me, I give it my all and go out there and do it. >> Uh, the first thing that popped out to me was uh that everybody play fast and violent. told um you know we said we said edge is hard and uh we play fast and we play violent. That's the thing that popped out to me the most. Um I feel like I could play a lot of the positions across the D line uh like coach said on on on early downs like first and second on the edge and uh having that ability to go inside on third downs uh is is where I see myself for sure. Carell, Paul Kohhurski, you you spoke yesterday briefly about Brian Hartline. Could could you give us some more detail and depth about his impact on you, kind of the the the nitty-gritty about how he affects Ohio affected Ohio State receivers and you in particular? >> Uh, Coach Arlline has done a great job with us, a phenomenal job with all the receivers that came out of Ohio State. Mike, this is for you. That's why they're being taken in in the first round. Um so that's why we're very confident that um that they're going to be able to contribute. >> For Mike, for Mike and Robert, if you could please both answer. Kell Keldrick's talked about that. Could you talk about the degree of projection that you're doing and and what you thought as as you scouted them about their production in college? >> Yeah, I I Paul I think you're always looking for um you know obviously the upside and every every situation is different um no matter what position they're playing or or what the scheme is and the talent and and you know um we certainly think they're they're going to be very productive at this level. Both of these guys being really young. How much a part of the evaluation was that? >> Yeah, I think that can be certainly a part of it. Um you know, these guys were 20 years old last year playing. Um and so that's certainly a part of it. You know, we think there's there's there's obviously room to grow with every player that enters the league. They have to develop more. Um, but certainly with these guys, I mean, um, you know, they they have, uh, you know, a lot of potential here to to get even better than they are right now. For sure. >> Carell, this team last year lacked for explosive plays, especially in the pass game. Obviously being picked at number four overall, they're going to expect you to provide some of that. What are some of the ways you feel like you can bring explosiveness to this offense? the same way I bring explosiveness and uh at the collegiic level, just going out there making the most of my opportunities and showing the team that they can trust me and put the ball in my hands more and more. >> Last few >> uh Ben Arthur, NFL on Fox, uh Carnell, this is for you. Um who are the receivers that you've tried to take bits and pieces from their game and maybe incorporate into yours? Uh Stefon Diggs and even C Red who's here. And then the mentality of football is just go out there and make the most of it. And then also just what happens when the ball come your way. So just learning from each other and perfecting our own routine. >> And also about that press coverage. >> Oh yeah, press in the NFL in the league. You just got to know how to win or one-on-one coverages. So that's all it's about. You got to take that very personal. The team's going to rely on you to go out there and win that oneonone match up with the top corner on the other side of you. So that's very personal. And the and the biggest thing in the in the league is can you win uh one to one coverage. So yeah, >> this is this is for both of you again. You guys known each other before last night and what was the plane ride like? What's it kind of like knowing that you're kind of in this together moving forward? >> Uh shoot. I seen him one time before. Uh we shot basketball together, but that's about it. Um plane ride. Playing ride was cool. like um man it's uh it's exciting like to to have this this kind of caliber player uh you know get drafted in the first round with me is uh is a blessing in itself and I'm I can't wait to get to get to know him and uh you know get to be a teammate for him. >> Yeah, that's how we met. We met on a uh on a little trip. He carried me a basketball. He was out there shooting those out there disappointing them. So yeah, and then for them we just chopped it up. Yeah. >> You played basketball in high school, didn't you? I did. >> How'd that turn out? Y'all have any 101 action? >> Oh, no, no, no, no. We ain't doing no. >> Last one. >> Uh, this question is for Robert. Um, yesterday Kellendrick had a pretty candid moment where he said he didn't know much about the Titans or the NFL in general. How much of maybe that transparency and accountability at such a young age fits the culture that you guys are trying to build here? >> No, for sure. That's a good one. Um, you know, transparency is everything. Communication is everything. um being able to speak your mind and have confidence that you can walk right into your coach's office and tell them what's on your mind and uh try to try to nip whatever negativity is flowing through your head. Just try to try to get it out and try to get it solved. So, um you know what, he's they're both extremely young, which is awesome. Um they're both haven't even scratched the surface of what we think they're capable of. And um and and Mike hit it on the head um in his opening statement. These two are elite character men who have elite work ethic and um they're they're going to find a way to get better. They're going to maximize who they are. >> All right. Thanks, guys. Jersey sub. Get some pictures.

title: David Bailey & Omar Cooper Jr. Introductory Press Conference (4/24) | New York Jets
text: question. >> What's the last 24? Well, really, uh, 12 hours been like for you, >> man. It's been fantastic. It's not >> on everyone. I'm getting mic. You get mic. Um, so at prior to my pro day, uh, the Jets, I had a dinner with them and Reich was actually there and I was sitting there and I was looking at him a little funny and I was like, you know, you look famili familiar and then he was like, yeah, like I was I was coaching at Stanford uh with with Luck. So >> David, did you get to know uh Arll at all throughout this process or did you have a history with him? You got to remember, you know, Omar and the personnel staff, they've been working on this, you know, for 12 months. Um you're we're new staff, you get in place, so we're later to the game. you know, didn't know a whole lot. I didn't know a whole lot about Max two months ago. And so, as you know, the you know, you go through the process with the with the staff. I mean, he's someone that I know just with between myself and the offensive line coaches. We've been talking a lot about him lately. >> Mike, how do you see his background in soccer and basketball before he committed to football show up and his footwork and his game? Oh, I just I think the biggest thing when you watch lineman play, you know, you know, you want to see him strike and stick and and with that, you know, the balance in the footwork, you know, his ability to stay alive on second and third reaction when he does engage. I think it's it's all over the video. >> You also talking about flexibility uh with your offensive linement. Is that good to because the injuries in the NFL kind of squared across the board. Was that good that you can plug people in in and out of your offense and keep on going in case of injury? >> Yeah, def. Yes, definitely. It's it's I think it's it's value that that that you you definitely look into especially when you get down to the 53man roster because you know it's one thing for your nine 10 ever how many linemen you keep each year um to play on a 53 but how do they get up on a 48? So uh position flex is very very important you know the second third center you know the fourth tackle that I mean that's those are all important conversations those are the conversations you have internally and uh so anytime I know from from my perspective as a coach and the evaluation process I I hold position flex the value of it very high >> did you all consider moving up or was it always the plan to stay where you were at 21? you know, we we we uh like I mentioned the other day, we field calls, you know, we all talk and um you know, there were some opportunities to move up, there's some opportunities to move back and um it just we just, you know, didn't want to trade away from this player. It just felt good. >> Was there a moment where he really got on your radar? >> What's that? >> Is there a moment where he really got on your radar? Can you remember like a moment where he's where he really stood out to you? Yeah, I I would say um really when we were going through our February draft meetings, that's really when he he uh you know, and the scouts came back. I wasn't at the Senior Bowl when the scouts came back and we started talking about the guys that were there and um uh and then you know, we got to our February meetings and that's that's when he really really grabbed our attention there and it just he just kept getting better and better for us with him. >> Guys, two more. Two more. >> One more. Since Andy came on in 22, you guys have spent a lot of early draft capital on offensive lineman. How reflective is this of kind of his entire strategy that he had at previous destinations? >> Uh from pre I mean you'd have to ask Andy that question, but I mean I think from uh day one we've said uh you know those big guys are important to us. >> Omar uh Bill and Noeo is similar in in experience and size. >> Did you see any of that? >> You said an owl. Would you say? >> Yeah. Illinois similar that he was inexperienced and tall. >> Yeah. I mean, from the experience standpoint, maybe a little bit, but I mean Al was uh 6'9. I mean, he was uh so um but yeah, there's this kid's uh football is ahead of him. I mean, he's only going to get better and better. Like I said, it's it's the more he plays, he's such a talented football player, and you know, he hasn't played a lot of football and I'm just excited about the future holds for him with us. title: Rueben Bain Jr.: ‘My Game is Vicious' | Press Conference | Tampa Bay Buccaneers
text: Well, uh, to start things off, we're obviously thrilled to death to have to get Ruben and to have his family here and to share this day with him. It's awesome that you guys could all come. That's it's really cool. Um, you know, we put a lot of work into all of our draft. Um, the players that we're looking at, it starts a long time ago. So, I mean, it's hard not to see this guy on the field when you're watching him even as a young, you know, the first time he played there. So, goes way back, but I'd be lying if I said yesterday that Todd and I were going in the draft thinking that there would be a a good chance of getting Ruben. So, you know, a lot of times we say surprises suck, but this surprise did not suck. Um, so you know, I said a lot last night, so I'll just kind of turn it over to coach, but once again, just very, very excited to have you and welcome to Tampa. >> Yes, sir. >> Uh, you know, it's like Jason said, you know, we we pick out a few guys that we don't think is going to make it to 15. And there were about eight or nine of them that regardless of position, we said if these guys end up falling, we're taking them without a doubt. and we had our minds made up on another player uh just because we figured the top eight or nine guys would be gone and we knew Ruben was a top 10 pick and he started falling a little bit and he caught the 15 and we knew it wasn't going any further and we couldn't be happier because of the mindset we're trying to change this year with the type of players we signed in free agency and the type of play that he does and the attitude he plays with and the force he plays with. It was really a no-brainer and he fit everything we're trying to do and get back to from a mental physicality standpoint and his play shows that and it was an easy decision. >> Um, how y'all doing? I'm excited to be here and let's get it started. >> This might be the biggest cheering section that we've ever seen for a introductory press conference. How special is it to have camp family in Tampa, but then also family that can very easily drive up from Miami? >> Uh, I feel like it's a once in a lifetime kind of thing for me. Um, something I don't take for granted knowing that I could have I could have been across the country somewhere, some way, somehow and God put me here and I don't take that for granted cuz I know my family's here and they going to support me each in every step of the way. Um, I only got 10 today, but you can see about 20 or 30 more rolling in from time for me being here. Toby, you look at at Ruben's game. You can play left side, right side, inside. How much is that versatility really appeal to you? Probably be an outside linebacker for you, but he's got the capability to do a lot more. >> It feels a great deal that he can move up and down the line of scrimmage. Obviously, he had great coaching in college and high school. So, it to be versatile in this game when you're only allowed to take so many to the game, it's very important to play at a couple different positions, and he can do that. How was there a point where where you realized that that Ruben was really possible and viable for 15? I don't know what what team he went past when you realized he really could. >> It was a possibility. I would say around 13. It was a possibility. You know, you don't take any of these things for granted because people can trade in front of you and everything else. So, you know, when it got to 15, I felt better, you know, but there was a possibility around 13. Todd, how satisfied are you to have brought in an edge rusher here with this 15 pick? I mean, how obviously he's talented? You guys talked about his skills, but just in general to address that position so early. How beneficial would that be for your defense? >> It's beneficial that we addressed it with him. Uh there's a bunch of edge rushers in this draft. Not many can play like he plays and it plays with the attitude he plays with and the heavy hands he plays with and fits the scheme that we play with as well as the people that's down there with him that he's going to be working with. >> We heard Jason last night talk about some of the traits that he really found attractive in him. But for you, what is it the bend? Is it the lower center of gravity? What is it about him physically that makes him such an asset to your defense? It's his physical style of play from a mental standpoint and a physical standpoint. Uh pass rushers come in different ways and different types and different sizes. Some are power, some are speed, some have an arsenal, you know, some can bend, some can't. He can do it all. He can do it all. And he shows that up and down the line of scrimmage. But he plays with a mentality and a no no losing mentality at all times. and he he fights and he plays with the right kind of attitude that and mentality that we're trying to bring to this team. >> Ruben in talking to Mario and others, you know, ever since you got there, you're the first guy, you know, didn't have to tell you to be early to meetings, didn't have to tell you to stay late as you did every day after practice. Where does that work ethic come from? Where where does that that burning desire come from? Um, I think just uh my family um having that that standard being put in front of me since I was adolescence and and a kid. Um really uh respect to my big brother. Um he the one that kind of showed me where football could take me. Uh he probably don't even know that but that's the biggest motivator in my life. Um giving me the constant motivation to get up and get after uh since I was a little kid running around at his high school practice, little kid running around his college practice. just happy to be there and there was a lot of lessons I took from that and now fast forward to today those lessons is what helped me be who I am today. >> When you play with a a nasty edge and a mean streak where does that come from and was there a point in time in your football career where that that switch was flipped. >> Uh I think I always had uh that kind of uh mindset. I feel like I kind of piggybacks off that question as well. Just from what I what was put in front of me um allowed me to be the player I am today. allowed me to kind of play with that that that that head on fire mentality. Um, and just run around knowing that you never know what play could be your last. So, I'm always play I'm always play it like that. Um, I come in with the game and the mindset that I don't take anything for granted. So, when I step on the field, I'm trying to give them all each and every time. >> Ruben, you said last night that you were going to speak with David. Did you have that conversation with him? How'd that go? Uh, I haven't yet cuz my phone been just so crazy. But I got to speak with Kaja and I just told him, man, I'm I'm be in this in his ear each and every day just latching on so I can get as much help as I possibly can because I'm trying to come in and help the team out as much as I possibly can. >> You were sorry. Uh, Ruben, you wore that number four really well at Miami. Um, are you gonna maybe try to apply if you're never here or is there >> Um, I've been told it's already it's it's already took it's busy right now, but uh, honestly, this is whatever they end up giving me. Uh, I'm a little frugal, so all that buying the jersey stuff off people, I I probably won't do that. Just take what they give me and go play some football. >> And there are a lot of Bucks fans that are also Miami fans, right? So, like, how excited are you to kind of maybe become a fan favorite here early on and and play in front of them? >> Uh, very excited. Uh, it's, like I said, it's opportunity. I don't take for granted. Um I got to come up here and see a game. I didn't get to play the game, but when we play USF, so I'm familiar with the the stadium, I'll say. But now this time, I actually get to strap up and be on the home side of things and and really just show people who I am, who I am, and I feel like they'll fall in love with that, and I'll fall in love with them. >> You said that you're the best player in the draft, best pass rusher, what have you, but in going to 15, I think that obviously Jason and Todd were very surprised you were still there. Does that put more of a chip that you've already got pretty big one on your shoulder anyway, but does that put more of a chip on your shoulder? >> Um, I mean, I'll say my mindset is always to have a bit of edge to me. Uh, I feel like I'm the best player no matter what. So, that's kind of what I feed into. Um, I really don't let any outside noise dictate that. I just kind of play with that mindset. I'm going to get it each and every play. for you being part of a program. Obviously Miami has a story history and and so many people fans in this area talk about like the glory days of the youth. I know you guys fell short of your ultimate goal, but to bring the program to where it was like what did that mean for you like personally to be part of that culture change? >> It meant a lot. Um especially for I know all the guys that was there throwing those five and seven, seven and six seasons. Uh it meant even more to us because we was there when it was ugly. We didn't just hop on the bandwagon when it was pretty. Um, so to actually build something from the ground up, I feel like it means a little bit more cuz Chris, he always says like he never wanted to say the US was back, but he was here. And that's a that's a mindset I have is we just doing what we do. We play football how we play and we going to reap the the rewards of our success. >> How did that force you to grow as a leader in and again being part of that culture change? >> Uh, it was it was challenging at first. Um, cuz just me, I'm more of a a quieter guy. Uh so understanding that is more than being uh by example kind of leader. Uh I have to be vocal at times. I'm still a little hesitant what I say because I feel like the the more selective you are with your words, the more the more weight it holds. Um so I kind of uh choose when it's the right time. But at all times I'm going to be a leader, whether that's being by example or vocal. He's a special talent, but what's the biggest adjustment for a guy coming from college even though he's dominated at the highest level to the NFL at that? >> It's really just the length of the season. You know, they we play 17 regular plus three preseason games than you got playoffs. And that's probably quite a bit more than they play in college. And as long as you come in in shape, and I'm sure he will. And he's probably already in shape, he'll be fine. It shouldn't be much of an adjustment. Ruby, I know players are motivated anytime you don't get picked by a team, but to be from Miami, to have starred at Miami, to have the Dolphins make another pick, how much will that motivate you? >> Uh, I mean, I feel like won't change anything. Um, my motivation is myself. I always want to be the best player on the field no matter what. Uh, no outside factors going to kind of weigh into that. And I'm going to play the game just as if I was playing anybody else. Um, and that's with all my effort. And when you see that, people gonna see the kind of player I am. >> Just so you know, the States passed on. >> Yeah, they did. >> Something that was talked about yesterday is just how much your passion for football sticks out. Has it always been like that or was there a moment that really for you? >> Ah, um, it kind of developed a little bit more when I was 13. I really didn't like football. I thought I was going to be a basketball player growing up, especially watching LeBron. He was in Miami at the time. So, I thought I was going to be a basketball player. But after uh I felt like I stopped going, it just showed me that football going to be the thing for me. And um that's when I felt like I really starting to understand what football could do and how to really like take pride in my game and what it really really means to be a defensive lineman. And ever since then, the sky's has been the limit. >> Jason was asked about your arm length last night. He said rather defiantly that Mike Tyson also had shorter arms, too. And I believe in an interview with my friend Cameron Wolf, he would also mention Mike Tyson. he came up. Is he is he some type of an inspiration for you athletically? >> Uh I don't know if people know but I really love boxing and so uh that's a person I feel like very vicious and violent and I feel like my game is vicious and violent. So it's some sort of comparison of mindset things uh I feel like we have in common and that's just uh I feel like it's a a great comparison. Speaking of competition, battles, looking forward to going against some guys in training camp like a Tristan Wors, a Luke Geti. >> Uh, for sure. Uh, the first thing I was thinking of was I could get better each and every day knowing I'm going against the best of the best. Uh, Tristan, I feel like he going to give me the best the best looks I possibly can. I'm going do my best to give him the best looks he possibly could get. Uh, because one, I know that that's a great caliber of player and I'm understanding that I ain't sharp as I am. That's what we was built on in college and that's my same mindset to come in and do the same thing at this level. Give him my all so I can get get all his from him. >> What are some words of advice you have for young guys that want to be where you are today? >> Uh to keep working. Um because nobody can never tell you no. It's never knows. It's not yet. Um nobody determines what you can and can't accomplish and and no matter what the situation no matter what the situation is, you always determine the outcome. Ruben, you learned a lot from Jason Taylor in your time here at Miami. Is there a top takeaway? What's what's the one thing top of mind that he taught you that he still? >> I can say uh like patience. Um and that really a lot like relate on to not only but life but football. I used to kind of tense up a little bit if I felt like games weren't really going my way. And so he uh instilled the mindset in me to rather just let things come to me and let let the game just flow and like my instincts just took over. >> How much did it help you to and how much did you learn and learn from each other? You're able to play with a guy like me in Miami. >> Uh that was a tremendous amount of help. Um coming into college was my mentor, somebody that took me under his wing and uh really introduced me to what college football is like. Uh, and I was able to really get one-on-one coaching because he was hurt that first year, my freshman year. And, um, ever since then, we just been flourishing and getting better each and every day. And come fast forward to this year, it was more of a still it's still a big boral relationship, but more like a peer right now. Um, and we was able just to really bounce off each other withformational competition, anything we really wanted to do. Anything >> else? Thank y'all.

title: Rueben Bain Jr.: ‘If You’re Not My Teammates, I Hate ‘Em’ | Press Conference | Tampa Bay Buccaneers
text: Hey, Ruben, congratulations. Uh, I don't know where you expected to go in terms of the first round. Can you just give us your reaction about the Buccaneers taking you and and remaining in the state of Florida? >> Uh, such a relief, man, knowing that I was fortunate enough to get my name called tonight, no matter where it was. Uh, having my name having my name called been a dream for the last 17 years. And so, actually having seeing this and hearing it come true, it's it's a it's a great feeling. and just the cherry on top of staying in Florida, man. I have family members that stay in uh Tampa. I have um former cousins that play for uh the Bucks. So, it's it's going to be a familiar atmosphere for me. Um and I'm just excited and stoked to get there. >> Who are your cousins that played for the Bucks? >> Carlton Davis. >> Boss. Yeah. Recent recent history. >> Yes, ma'am. >> Did you hear from Carlton after you got picked? Uh my phone's on D and D right now, so I know once I [laughter] get here, uh I'll be able to I'll be able to probably hear from you. >> You're gonna have to update us on how many messages you had once you finally get back to it. That's >> a lot. >> Hey, Ruben, what kind of interaction did you have with the draft with the Bucks during the draft process? >> Um I'll be honest, not a lot, but uh the ones I had, he wor um I told him, man, like I got family that stay in Temple, so it's going to be easy for me. It's going to be easy to transition. So let's do it. and coach Bulls did it. >> What do you know about Bull's defense and how do you think you're going to fit into it? >> I feel like I fit in just fine. Um coach Coach Bulls is an aggressive defensive like-minded coach and I'm an aggressive defensive like-minded player. So I feel like it's it's two and two put together. It's going to be real simple, real smooth. Now it's just about me learning plays, earning the trust of my teammates and learning what I can do to help the team. >> Kasha Kansas is from Miami. Do you do you know him? Have you? >> Yeah, real well. Real well. So, I know I know when I get him on my phone, it's going to be it's going to be a great conversation. >> What have the last couple weeks been like for you? Because you've had all this training and and buildup and then obviously the news surfaced a couple weeks ago about the accident in 2024. Like, how how did you kind of handle all that? How did you navigate that? I'm sure there's a lot of emotional highs and lows that that really go into that. And then leading up to this moment, >> uh, yeah, you know, everything has it ups and downs, but I I I just try to make everything simple as it could possibly be. Um, try to prioritize whatever I prioritize in the moment. And right now, that's is uh just football and and making sure I'm just really making as a main priority for me. Um, my days are kind of fairly simple. Just working out, going home, getting on the phone, and pretty much doing the same thing. And it's been a rinse and repeat kind of cycle. Ruben, when it comes to football, what would you say is your best trait in terms of what you bring on the field and also maybe in the locker room? >> My motive, I feel like my motor and my mindset is contagious cuz when people see me, how I play and how I care about the game of football kind of spreads off on other people and I actually have proof of that and that's not me just talking. That's from high school all the way up into college. >> How did working with Jason Taylor at the U prepare you to play at this next level? >> Can you repeat that one more time, please? working with Jason Taylor, how did that prepare you to play at the next level? >> I felt like I got the best the best coaching I could possibly get these last three years. I mean, it's Hall of Fame coaching. I don't really realize until I look back on it or hear somebody else talking about it. Um, so now it's just a amazing opportunity and I was blessed enough to get that that style of play, that style of coaching for the last three years. And not too many people can say they had one position coach all the whole college career and mine was a Hall of Famer. So, it's just even more cherries on top. >> Well, I mean, in so much of our pre-draft, like leadup as media members, we're talking about you and we're talking about your teammate Hakee Meador because both of you guys I mean, it's rare to have two guys, you know, at the same position in in one draft class that are both being talked about as as potential first round picks. >> Oh yeah, man. It's very rare, but we did, man. That's a credit to us. That's a credit to coach Chris Paul, coach Taylor and and how we came about our work each and every day on the green tree whether I was in any stadium home all way. We care about football so much and I feel like you seen it in our play and and God just had the results that that came out tonight. >> What was the feeling like to walk across the stage, meet the commissioner, hear your name called in Pittsburgh. What was that feeling emotion like for you? >> It was awesome. U something I dreamed of, like I said, for the last 17 years of my life. So, actually getting to actually getting to go through with it. Um, it was amazing. Not too many people get invited to the draft. Uh, so it wasn't I took it wasn't something I took for grinning. Every every second I was here, I love them because I knew there'd be people be that's dying to be in my seat right now. >> And I heard your family has coordinated outfits. How did that all come about? >> Uh, it's just idea I came up with. Um, we kind of was able and fortunate enough to kind of pull it off and I feel like we all look coordinated and smooth. >> Oh yeah. >> How much has your family support meant to you throughout this trip? A >> lot. It means the world to me. I have about 20 to 25 family members up here today. Um, and five of those stay in Tampa. So, I know I have a a great support system that's going to be there. So, anybody I need to lean on, they're automatically there. Then my family's only three hours away. Uh and um I feel like everybody knows Tom Brady because Tom Brady um Mike Evans because what he do is Mike Evans. Um it's just I've been fortunate enough to know people. Um, like I say, my cousin Clark and Levante David, he's been there for a long time. So, I'll be able to get on the phone with him after this and just get the best uh I feel like opinion and best review. >> So, so that's a name that you need to drop around here very very frequently. Leavante David. He's he's very well thought of and >> you talk to Sav. He was actually just at the spring game. So, I know you're gonna have something to say when you see me. [laughter] >> Anything else? Congratulations, Ruben. Congratulations, Ruben. Y'all have a good night.

title: Jason Licht on Selecting Rueben Bain Jr.: 'Very Excited' | Press Conference | Tampa Bay Buccaneers
text: We got our guy. >> Jason, I think a lot of people would say this is a top 10 player that that slid down to 15. Is is this just too good to pass up? >> Yeah, absolutely. Um, now time will tell. You know, we think very highly of him. Obviously, think he's a great player. you know, there were very few scenarios where we thought he'd be there, but um there was scenarios um and we're very excited. So, it's uh I've probably never seen a more excited draft room. >> What do you like best about his game? >> Um I love he's very unique where he's got a un great blend of power and athleticism. He can bend. Um he's got get off. He's very powerful. He's got very uh explosive uh not just athleticism but powerful hands, powerful uh strength. Um and he plays very edgy. Yeah, he plays with a chip on his shoulder. You guys do extensive work on these prospects and obviously for us news surfaced, you know, less than two weeks ago about the motor vehicle accident that he was involved in in 2024, but you've done a lot of work on him as a person. What What can you tell people that maybe have concerns about him? >> Well, we've been doing work um we'll start the process for next year's draft next week. So, our scouts, um, shout out Caesar, uh, Rivera. Um, he's been on it for a long time. We've known about this for a long time now. I know I know it just came out a couple weeks ago. It was a it was a very tragic, um, accident, um, tragic experience for for the family. And it's it's, you know, it's something you never want to see happen. But um you know he's he's a good person. Um was involved in something that uh you know none of us ever want to be involved in and um never want any of our loved ones to be involved in. So but um you know he loves football. He loves football. >> He was coached by Jason Taylor, Pro Football Hall of Famer um who has called him a professional. the way that he approaches that uh when you when you see his production and when he gets that type of professional level tulage, does that just make the decision even better when when you hear comments like that? Yeah, you love to be able to draft players that come from great programs and have been coached very well. And I know our coaches have a very good uh relationship, a lot of our coaches do with with Jason and um we've been talking we obviously talk with him and and you know we like we do all prospects and their coaches but to to draft a player that's come from a program like that that's uh you know excellent program to say the least uh it's just makes the process a little bit easier. Um, and you have a little bit more faith in, you know, the development of the >> Jason, you know, I'm sure you looked at me, too, but like this guy's only 21 years old. To get a guy that's that young that has that big of a ceiling, how how encouraging is that? >> Yeah. No, it's it's it's great. You know, like I I think I told you guys before, we we I mean, you you don't necessarily factor age. Um, but you know, it's something and uh, you know, it's one step at a time. He he still has to come in here. We're not anointing him the, you know, into the Ring of Honor or Hall of Fame yet, but uh, but, you know, we certainly like everything about him and we're very excited about it. >> What do you think his addition does for Yabi on the other side? Well, I think you know, you add a player like Reuben and he does what we hope he can do and think he can do. I should say think, not hope. You can redact that. Um he um it opens a lot of things up. It makes everybody along the D line better when you can have two, you know, edge presence presences. Um you know, the the line the protections don't slide as much. You have to decide where to slide them. um opens things up. So I think it's you know potentially now we we David Walker you know we have you know we have we have a arsenal there right now that um we feel good a very good rotation. So um with with Quan and you know still have Nelly and all that it's you know you can't have too many. I say it every year but then it just doesn't work out that we can draft one at a premium but now we did. So, um hopefully um hopefully we can reap the rewards here. >> When you're when you're looking at these guys and then ultimately setting your board, you're not just looking at the player, you're looking at the person. Your locker room that you have right now is proof of that. What was it that convinced you that he was a Buccaneer man? >> Um his passion for the game, his passion to want to be the best. Um, we like his his edge that he brings out there and you know the guy practices the same way that he plays and football is, you know, one of the most important things in his life. >> When you look at the arm length is what it is, right? It's shorter than than 31 in. Kalasha Cany doesn't have the longest arms. How does does Bane overcome that? Is it is it just the the quick speed to power? Is it the the ability to dip and rip and and avoid the offensive tackles? How does he overcome that for you on tape? >> I think one of his um assets is his low center of gravity and his power, his strength and his um urgency. I mean, Mike Tyson had short arms, too. So, um you know, he tries to win every every rep, and he usually does. Jason, is that doesn't always line up so well that your most obvious positional needs line up with the best player. So, we had some teams seeing if we wanted to go back, but once uh he was there, I didn't want to risk that uh scenario. So, I waited a couple minutes, but it uh >> You mentioned that you were surprised. Maybe not surprised, the right word, but you're glad he was there, obviously. Um, why do you have a theory as to to why he was still there? Like do you think it was any of the stuff that's come out? Do you think it's his character? Um there's some really good football players uh that went in front of him and there's, you know, we had a a quarterback that went >> and then we had, you know, some offensive linemen and >> pushed him down >> and pushed him down a little bit and it's goes to show you that, you know, a lot of teams have a lot of needs and you know, your board is, you know, you try to set it best the best available player, but you know, it always enters your mind when you have needs and this one, you know, we had them we had them very high up on the court. So, um, probably would have took him a lot earlier. So, >> when did you think he might really be in play? I mean, the Cowboys took downs, you know, but was that maybe >> I think it was around then. Yeah. >> Jason, in your in your call with him because he's he slid further down than many thought and all the stuff that has kind of been coming up recently. Did you get a sense in your conversation that he comes in with an extra added edge motivation to him because of this maybe night didn't play out exactly how he thought it might go? >> Well, keep in mind it was a pretty short call and he was very emotional as we were. Um and um he was just very very grateful that uh that he was coming here. So I think I asked him first thing was picked up the phone. I said, "What are you doing the next 5 to 10 years?" He says, "I'm going to be a buck." And he was he was very emotional. So I wanted him to I didn't want to get into a deep conversation with him and neither did Todd. I wanted him to celebrate with his family. And I know that's a big night for him. >> What what what does that mean for you on a personal level when you get to make a phone call like that? And then on top of the fact that I'm sure he's been dealing with a lot over the last two weeks obviously like that's that I'm sure it's been an emotional roller coaster for him >> to make that call in a way that says, "Hey, we see you like and we want you here." >> Yeah. Well, it's Yeah. I' I've never received that call. So, I can't tell you how he uh how he uh how he feels, but I can only imagine. It's It's got to be uh you know, it's been a long process for these guys. a lot of visits, a lot of training, combine, all that stuff. For it to to come to an end for I mean this that process come to an end, it's got to be a relief. But then also just I think he was genuinely very excited to be a Buck. So I know a lot of former Bucks have already reached out to me. So it's it's it's a >> What was Todd's reaction or statements in there? He was just very excited. You know, he's a hell of a football player and he's uh the type of player that we've been kind of focused on here um to bring in and um so he was he was very excited. Todd keeps it pretty close to the vest. He was pretty excited though. >> You said former Bucks contact you uh was sat one of them. >> Well, my phone is buzzing right now as we're talking so I'm sure he'll be one of them soon. Um, so it's uh it's a lot. It's a lot. >> Anything else? >> Jason, last year you mentioned uh Mechco Ibuka was a top 10 talent when you took him at number 19.
