title: Head Coach Dan Quinn Talks LB Sonny Styles | Command Center | Commanders | NFL
text: Fellas, we got the game plan crew back together again. Welcome in our head coach, Dan Quinn, who has been very, very busy, man. Getting your guy in round one. We saw your excitement when we drafted Sunny Styles, man. You even had a little curse word to say to the camera. That was so fly. But he was also excited to be here. He said >> this morning, I told my parents, I'mma be a commander. I don't care what nobody else says, man. How happy are you to have a guy like that in the building? >> It was awesome. And uh it speaks to maybe the environment that collectively everybody's creating here >> and it's one about like absolutely putting it all in to be your best and that's at every part not just coaches and players but everybody pouring into one another to see how far we can take it and you have good standards like that and people want to be a part of it um I think there's no telling where it can go. >> So coach I mean obviously you were excited I was excited. BC was excited. It was it was exciting time. The thing that got me was like I thought there was no way he was going to get there at seven. Obviously Tennessee drafts the receiver. When did you start to kind of say maybe our guy is going to be there at seven? >> It was after the fourth round pick. >> And so then you go right into what's the first rule of Fight Club? You don't talk about >> Don't talk about Fight Club. >> And so okay, there's a chance here that this could go down. And uh so then they're waiting. Trade comes in with Kansas City. just again fight club rules, right? >> And uh so then you know once that happened uh you know Adam was right there already had the number on the postit and uh cleared way for the phone call to take place and so >> um it was such a uh clear representative like you put so much in the ball what he can bring to our team and uh yeah really pumped to have him here >> and coach a little earlier you said what we're building here and that is what Sunny Styles talked about. I got to interview him right after he was drafted and he said the people in the building he said that's what made me buy in Ohio State that's what made me buy into here. How happy does that make you that the culture you've built in such a short time is permeating like that where all these players free agents as well come in and say this is the place I want to be. Yeah, 26 feels like um a new start in some ways and sometimes you don't need a new place to have a new start. And so the 25 season was so difficult for a lot of us. And so to have some of the free agents, you feel their energy coming in, having, you know, draft picks like Sunny coming, being a part of it. There is a freshness that goes with that. Uh we're excited that he's here. We're excited what he's where he's going. And like we're also excited like to be on this journey with him, >> you know, to see where he can get to because I really think it's going to be a bar that's super high and uh that's something that you want to strive for as a coach to say, can we take him to that place? >> You talked about something I think is interesting is like where he's going. You know, when AP was in here yesterday, he talked about like from the first game to the last game of last season, you saw a dramatic improvement. When you cut on the tape of him at Ohio State, like what do you see from him? I think the speed and the violence of action, those are the things that jump out to me because >> just gave me chills right there. >> Speed and violence. Love that. >> Like there's a specific play um you know watching it just Saturday night. I was just reviewing and I can remember watching my iPad. I was sitting next to Stace and I was like damn. And she's like what? I showed her the play. It was against Illinois and it was a four- yard game but he was a curl player going to and the the explosion on the running back to knock him out of bounds was just remarkable. So the four-yard gain of that, it wouldn't have shown up anywhere on the stat sheet, but the speed, the finish, the balance that it was there, it's a over and over again, can you train somebody into that space because not everybody has that in their body to be able to do it. And so you combine that with the work ethic, the humility, how much he loves the game, like you put all that together, you really get fired up about what it could be. >> Yeah. And I think when you talk about what it could be, I see a guy at Ohio State who's in multiple spots. like he's kind of playing like a pseudo nickel position. He's on the ball, he's off the ball. How important is that flexibility for you and in the Serant Jones defense? >> Yeah. Anytime you you played another position a good bit of your career, like so he was a defensive back. Yeah. >> You know, coming up through high school and two years at college where he played safety. So being in that room and the communication, the techniques that go involved with it, now you get to apply those skills to a different position, you're already elevated at those skills. covering man-to-man, knowing zones, how to play that. >> That's a unique thing that you're able to do and bring. And so, the best linebackers have the >> for sure the speed and the athletic ability to play safety. And so, I'm glad that he got two years to develop and hone those skills because it happens so much quicker. The line of scrimmage, the blocks that get to you differently. And so, you to really improve you have to have self-awareness. And I asked him in specific, what did you want to see better from 24 and a 25? And it was like clearly demonstrated. >> That's cool. >> And all those things you mentioned, you're hearing that versatility. That's what Dvonte Jones came in here and said he wanted. He wanted players like that. So I have to ask that reaction from Donte Jones. We know you were excited. What did Donte Jones say when y'all got this guy? >> Low key. He you know he gets excited, but he's not. He's like smiling and you can see that brain already working. He gave a just a fantastic overview um on the first day with the veterans here this week about the defense and what it could look like. I think it's important for all ball players to zoom out. All right, what's the identity? How are we going to play and then zoom back into the specific skills. And so what I like about this is he's adding into a strong group the speed that we've added through the off season from at linebacker with Leo and Odaf and Casey and now you're adding Sunny as well and Frankie and Jordan and the speed that I'm hoping to see from our defense. I think there'll be a remarkable difference. >> And it seems like you got kind of a fun unique challenge with that, you know, middle level of the defense. You got three dudes who are really unique athletes. Like they can rush, they can cover, they're physically violent like you were talking about. Like how do you make sure that all kind of works and like you know what is your hand in that kind of >> I've been through that some other times before and the best way to teach some of it is just by concept. So you may have the safety position, but this is the technique or this linebacker. And so safety's at linebacker, linebacker's at safety ends who can play down on the line. So when you teach the concept, it doesn't matter what we letter the person. It's can you do this skill? It's kind of like in basketball, can a big guy, you know, bring the ball up? Yeah, if he can. You don't have to just, you know, give it to somebody else. So, it's those types of things that allow identifications to be difficult for an offense. Knowing like why is this person over here and not to the where he's supposed to be and then blitz them or play him from off and there's a disguise. And if you can put mental and physical pressure on the offense, that's really what you're looking to do. And we definitely have the speed to now put the physical. So, the scheme has got to put the mental pressure on. That's how you can really affect an offense. And it's cool to hear you talk about that because that's something that's becoming more in vogue, right? Is like this you're teaching concept. Yes. Is that something Donte is bringing with him here? Because that's that's really exciting, I think. >> Yeah, I think it's important. Think of all the offenses that can check things at the line of scrimmage and offenses have been ahead of defenses for a few years in that way of finding the best look, finding what they want to run. And so now defenses are starting to catch up, putting people in different locations, having their own checks and balances at the line of scrimmage. So the offense doesn't get into a premier play against a look they want. And so the defenses are now >> checking that as well. And so you have to have versatile players, Logan, to do that because what you may your responsibility at the start of the play may be different when you check it. >> Yeah. Yeah. >> And think of a run to a pass on offense. well, could be simple as like a blitz to a coverage on defense. And so having the ability to have versatility certainly allows you to do that. >> And coach, you've talked about wanting to bring guys in here that are commanders, that have a certain type of pedigree, a certain type of morality, if you will. And we know a guy in Sunny Styles. He's only 21. Yes. >> But he shows that leadership quality. He wore the number zero Ohio State. We know what that means. Talk to me about the person that is Sunny Styles and made you say he's the perfect fit for Washington. Yeah, he's definitely has a um some traits of football, the preparation, the um like the game, the like what he takes care of his body, the training that the great players have. And so we won't compare him to, you know, great players because it's important for him to go on his own journey. I don't want him to be somebody else, but he has the traits of the great players that want to do the unrequired work, want to find it out, figure it out. And so, um, you know, like a guy like London, you know, who just finds any edge they can to say, "All right, >> this can happen." He has those type of traits about him. And those are the things that allow you to ascend really fast because like you're not going to take any other way than to figure it out. And so like he's figured a lot out. >> Yeah. And you you talked about how special he is, you know, like as a person. And I don't want to put any like expectations on him, but have you ever had a rookie signal caller for a defense in your career? >> Um we did it once in Atlanta with a linebacker named Dion Jones. >> Dude, Dion Devbo. Legend. Yeah. >> And uh so he was, you know, quick linebacker coming out and that was good. And the nice part about now Logan is because of the colleges are now doing that as well. Oh, with a with a radio. That's right. >> That helps because it's not as big a transition to go and do that, but um it does help that you can get into that spot to do that. And so if they're ready, um it's worth it >> to get that development. We did it with Wags. I wasn't there as rookie year, but Ken was and so he would be another linebacker that from the very beginning as a rookie. Um, let it, called it, and they became an excellent unit, you know, with Wags right in the middle of the communication hub of everything in Seattle. But when he got there, he did it right away. >> Coach, we appreciate your time. We know you're a busy, man, so we're going to let you get going cuz it's still >> tonight. Are you ready? You guys already I'm about to say I was about to ask you if you was going to give us a little bit of inside information. >> Hell no. >> That's not how we do it here in Command Atlanta. We appreciate you, coach. Game plan crew back together again, coach. Good luck tonight. >> Yeah, good to see you guys. >> Thank you, sir.

title: Sonny Styles First Interview as a Washington Commander | Command Center | NFL DRAFT
text: Command his family here with the number seven overall pick in the 2026 draft. Sunny Styles in the building here. Looking good in that burgundy and gold hat, my brother. First things first. Congratulations. >> Yeah, I appreciate it. I'm blessed. I just want to give all the glory to God, man. Super excited. Can't wait to get to Washington and get to work. >> Amen. Amen. And you were overcome with emotion when you found out about that pick, man. What hit you in that moment because you knew you were going at some point tonight, but that emotion still hit, man. What was that about? >> Man, you know, I had a lot of great visits. Um, you know, but when I was in that building, it was different. Coach Noran was different. Coach Jones was different. Coach Quinn, Mr. Peters, every meeting just felt different. It felt right. Felt like they had amazing people in the building all the way to like the player development staff. Everybody was just great people. Um, so I'm super excited to come to that building. And >> and you must have been excited cuz even the crew, you brought Richie rocking the burgundy suit. So there's a little bit of vibes there that maybe you were going to come to the burgundy and gold. Did you know that you would be coming here at number seven? >> I told my family this morning I was going to be a commander pick seven. They there told me a bunch of other teams. I was like, I'm telling you, I know what it is. I had a gut feeling. So, I'm just I'm excited it happened. It's the perfect fit. >> And you said during your visit, you told DQ, I hope I'm back here soon. What about Washington made it the perfect fit for you, >> man? Um, I think it's the people that that's what drew me to Ohio State. You know, obviously when you're getting recruited out of college, I mean, out of high school, you have to pick where you go. And, uh, the people is what drew me to Ohio State. And then with the commanders, it was the people. Um, Coach Quinn, Mr. Peters, a great man. Coach Jones a great man. Coach Doran's another great man. Like everyone I met, like I said in the building were great people, great men and women. Um, so that's really what drew me there. You know, I think I'm a I'd like to say I'm a good person and uh I like to surround myself by other good people. So I'm glad I get to come into that building. >> And a lot was made about your versatility about you being a former safety, which is wild to think that you can run a 4-3 being this massive. What is that versatility and that experience in multiple positions? Why does that make you the most dangerous person in this 2026 NFL draft? Yeah, I think when you are versatile and can do a multitude of roles for a defense, it makes the defense unpredictable, especially as a coordinator. You have a bunch of different chess pieces on the board, uh, it makes you makes you unpredictable, like I said. Um, you know, I think I can do a lot of things. And I think the, you know, the best part about me, I'm just scratching the surface. Um, you know, I'm super excited where I'm at right now, but there's still so much work to go. >> And last, but not least, you get to share this moment with your brother. He is here at the draft with you, man. How special is this, not only for you, but for your family who also sacrificed so much for you to get to this point? And me and him been working for this since we was 5 years old. Um, and I told my dad, I was like, "Hey, dad, you gonna cry today." He was like, "Man, I was up early in the morning, too." He's like, "This ain't no surprise." Um, so I think that perspective of it, like, it's no surprise being here, but, you know, obviously super blessed and appreciated to be here. >> And Sunny, we're going to let you celebrate cuz we know this is a big moment for you. We know your brother's still out there. Last thing, Commanders fans are all excited to have you here. Give a message to the fans on what they can expect to see when Sunny Styles on the field this year. >> Man, you're getting a guard loves the game. uh gonna be fast, violent, physical, and uh get better each and every week and just help the team win. >> Amen to that. We love winning, baby. Commanders family here with our number seven pick at Ohio State, Sunny Styles. Congratulations, brother. >> Yes, sir.

title: Introductory Press Conference: Sonny Styles Meets the Media as the Newest Washington Commander
text: I'll be brief today, but um I can tell you guys as impressive as he is on the field, he he's just as impressive off the field. And uh we're we're super excited to have him. Mom and dad, you guys did a great job. And so um just really really uh pumped to have him here. And uh really in short, Sunny embodies everything we look for in a commander on and off the field. So uh really thrilled, really excited. Uh, so please join me in welcoming Sunny Styles to the commander family and the DMV. >> How we doing? Uh, just want to say something real quick. I want to say thank you to He made me call him AP. I like to call him Mr. Pet. I'm going to say thank you to AP. Um, thank you to Coach Quinn, Mr. Paris uh for you guys believing in me, putting a lot of faith in me. You know, I think when I came in this building, you guys talked about like just scratching the surface. You talked about how there's so much more to unlock and uh you know, I see it. I see the vision. I'm excited to be here. Um I've been telling everyone this is where I wanted to be. Um so I'm super excited to be here and uh just can't wait to get to work. >> So start off. >> Name and affiliation. All right. Uh, Sunny John Kim, ESPN. I'm curious now that you're sitting up here as a first round pick, what was your reaction when you got moved to safety and then when did you feel you became a guy who could be a linebacker at this level? >> Yeah, so when I came in at safety my first two years, uh, it's kind of what I've been playing my whole life. Um, switched to linebackers my sophomore year. You know, I think when I got to the end of my sophomore year, I really wasn't where I wanted to be. Um, you know, I ended up switching, sitting down with the coach, head coach, coordinator. Felt like it was best for the team, felt like it was best for me. and uh you know I was happy to do it. You know I attacked the role, maximized the role, just wanted to help the team win and I think it worked out for me. >> Hi Sunny Liam Griffin with the Washington Times. You come from an NFL bloodline. I'm curious, is there any advice that your dad has given you about this experience and the transition going from college to the NFL? >> Yeah, he talked a lot about finding a vet in in the room. Uh whether it be on my side of the ball, on the offense, just finding a guy that you admire the way he works and uh you know kind of learning from him, you know, getting all the little little nuggets from him. Um, and just being a uh coming in with humility and uh the willingness to learn, open-minded. >> Hi Sunny. Um, Nikki Jafala with the athletic. Um, who helped you the most as you transition from safety to linebacker and how do you think your safety background helps you at that position? >> Um, I say helped me the most, I would say coaches, then my dad. Um, spent a lot of time watching ball with them. You know, my dad, he got his own stuff going on, but he'd come in the building and watch tape with me. Um, you know, obviously he's former linebacker, but then, uh, coach Lord Knight is obviously my position coach. You know, he put a lot of belief in me. You know, when I switched to linebacker, he texted me and said, "You're going to be a first-round pick." And, uh, you know, for him to say that after like my first two years playing safety, like it was okay. Like, I wasn't on a projection to be that yet. And, uh, you know, to hear that from your coach means a lot. So, you know, I was super happy, super happy when he did that. And, uh, yeah, I think those two guys are a big reason why I succeeded at the position. David Aldridge with the athletic. Welcome to DC. Um, you had a great talented defensive room at in Columbus. I just wonder how you guys, you and Caleb and Arll and how you guys kind of found a niche with one another so that you could play as a unit together. >> You know, I think it starts in the offseason. Um, you know, just training with each other, working out, getting to know each other, hanging out outside the building. Um, but I think, you know, at Ohio State, we had like-minded people. um guys who love football, love to win, love their brothers, and uh you know, I'm sure it's the same thing here. Um at least from what I see from the staff. So, um I think we have guys who are good people off the field and like-minded on the field. Uh good things happen and it's easy to gel. >> Hey, signing Donna Hopkins, Pro Football Plus. Welcome to the DMV. Uh this has been a long process through the combine, through the senior day now with the commanders. What has that process been like and what have you learned about yourself in that process? >> Um, you know, for me it's been fun. Uh, combine prep was awesome out in California training with guys, training with my brother, some of my teammates, some other guys from across the country. That was fun. Then you go to the combine, you got get to go out there, compete, you know, meet with a bunch of coaches, talk ball, talk about yourself, um, go to pro day, go on these visits, uh, and then obviously, you know, the draft day. Um, so it it's been fun. It's been great. And you know, I think I learned about myself that um I'm not anxious for the moment. You know, I'm excited. And you know, I think uh you know, talking to my dad, uh you can be excited and be anxietyfree when you know you put the work in. Uh so you trust that work and then get to this next level. You know, create a routine, create a regimen, and trust that work and just uh trust the process. >> Hi there, Candy Waller, Buoie TV. Um so can you just share what this last 24 hours have been like for you? >> Yeah. um yesterday morning just hanging out with a bunch of family. Uh my guys from Vayner, just soaking it all in. Um just enjoying each other, you know. I think uh Pittsburgh was only a three-hour drive, so I had a bunch of family down there and that was awesome. Then you go to the red carpet, green room. Um you know, honestly, everyone asked me all day like, "Am I anxious?" And I told everybody no. Like I was just excited. You know, I had a feeling I knew where I was going and it happened just like it was supposed to. Um, so it was a dream come true and obviously celebrate with the family after seeing all my other fellow Buckeyes get drafted was awesome. You know, we think we were all gym. We just super happy for each other. You know, everyone ended up right where they're supposed to be. >> Hey Sunny, Mitch Tesler, Moneyal Sports. Uh, with Arll going to to New York and Caleb going to Dallas. What are thoughts of playing those guys twice a year and what were those uh text messages like last night? You guys talk at all? >> Yeah, I saw him after in the hotel. You know, we're excited for each other. Can't wait to get to work. you know, obviously we're gonna get after him, so hopefully I can see him out there on the field. >> Hey, Sunny. Uh, Ben, standing with the team 980, the the scratching the surface comment. We've heard that, you just mentioned it a minute ago. What does that mean to you when when somebody says you're just scratching the surface? What do you kind of see as the vision for yourself? >> Yeah, I mean, I have high expectations for myself, you know? Um, I don't think the goal for my career was just to get to the NFL and that was it. Like, round of applause. You know, I think it's it's I'm happy to be here and I'm happy for the moment. Um, but there's still so much work to be done. You know, I was in year two at the position last year. I thought I played fairly well. Um, but I watch myself. I know I have so much more in the tank and, you know, in all facet of the game. There's so much more to work on. >> Hey, Sunny Les Carpenter at the Washington Post. Uh, just the way that you're kind of, you know, the presence you have right now and sort of the ease that you have in this. It's almost like you've been waiting for this day all your life. I mean, is is that kind of the way it is? I mean, you you do seem and you seem last night, too, very prepared for all of this and nothing seems to be phasing you right now. You know, I think I can uh attribute that to my parents. You know, uh they raised me the right way and uh you know, I think I've worked for this moment um to get here, get to this level and exceed at this level. Um so I think that's why I feel ready and uh no really no anxiety or anxiousness. You know, obviously, you know, being at Ohio State, they develop as as men and as players. Um so when you step into the building, you know, we're ready to be pros. Sunny, welcome to Washington DC. Chad Ricardo with Fox 5. I had to imagine that you've envision this moment for years and years and years. I wonder that now that you're here, how the dream of this moment correlates to the reality of it. Man, I think uh being a little kid um like the draft felt so like surreal and um you know it was amazing you know once you get your name called and all those things but uh I think once I got my name called it was like you walked on the stage experience all that then I was like now I'm ready to go to work like I'm just excited I'm excited for the next step I'm excited to get better I'm excited to you know help this team win. Hi Sunonny Heather Mcdana, NBC4. Welcome to Washington. You've you've mentioned that this is where you wanted to be and you met with a lot of teams who said a lot of wonderful things I'm sure about you about themselves. Why is this where you wanted to be? What stuck out about the commanders? >> Um, you know, I take it back to like when I was coming out of high school and uh I went to Ohio State, went in that building and it was great people in the building. Um, starting with Coach Day, the whole coaching staff, other players. Uh when I came in this building, first person I see, Coach Noran. Great energy. Um you could tell he's just a genuine guy, great man. Um then I could sit down with Coach DJ, Coach Jones, uh go talk to Coach Quinn, uh AP, and uh it was just great energy in the whole building, every single person I met with. And it just felt right. And uh that's why when I left this building, I was like, man, like this this is it. This feels right. And I was hoping it was going to work out the way it did. So, just super excited to be here. >> Hi, Sunny. Welcome to Washington. Skyler Nelson from the Washington Informer. There have been talks um about your leadership in when you were in Ohio. I think um you know just s getting a chance to sit down and talk to him and understanding like you know he's he's really driven and he's really you know has like the desire to be great and he wants to be great for us and and you could and you could feel that you know a lot of guys try to sell themselves and and rightfully so it's a job interview so that's part of it but um you know his was genuine his was real he wasn't and trying and is very comfortable in what he said. And so, um, it makes you really confident that, you know, he's he's going to do everything he can to to be great and be great for us. >> Adam, I know you obviously still have two days left in the draft, but you made a ton of additions on the defensive side of the ball through free agency and adding Sunny, obviously. How would you kind of assess the improvements that you made at all three levels on defense so far? Um, yeah, I think I think it goes back to kind of what we wanted to do, just get younger and faster. And I think we've done that. Um, but we've we've added a lot of guys that that we would call commanders. And so I think that's that'll never be um that'll be never be something that we don't do. That'll always be at the forefront of all of our decision- making. And so um you know, getting those guys and they've been in all week and I wish I'd been more present with with the team this week. I was I was not very present this week hold up in my office a little bit and uh but uh can't wait to hang out with those guys next week. But um just the the the little bit that I did get a chance to go down to lunch and and walk around the building and and these guys are all bought in. You know, the new guys that we've you know they're bought in. They're going to dinner together. They're staying late. They're they want to they really want to um you know, these guys really really want to be great and they really want to learn the new defense. Um, Donte, you know, I talked to a bunch of them and Dante has just blown them away, you know, just the way, you know, he presents in his teaching and and so they're really excited to learn the new defense and so um, they got new guys that are they're hungry. They're hungry to prove themselves and hungry to to to learn and so um, it's it's been really exciting to see. >> Hey, bud. Um, you mentioned Sunny as the person more than more than just the player and talk about getting to know his family. obviously comes from a football family. His brother's a player. His mother is fully ingrained in the football lifestyle. How how key is that for a young guy to be able to have success not just in a big-time college program, but also taking the step to the NFL? >> Yeah, you always, you know, I you want to bet on the the stock, you know, and bet on somebody who's been around it and somebody who who knows what it's what it's like. And so, um, that's that's always a bonus, not a requisite, but it's always it's always helps. and understanding even if you're not, you know, even when you're little, you just kind of understand like what it takes and and you can tell that his parents have instilled that in him just that his how mature and responsible and um you know driven he is. He's he's been raised really well, but at the same time like he's he's just like guy you want your daughter to marry. And so, um, you know, all of those things. And so, yeah, he's he's been raised really well and and certainly been around football. So, um, that that is a big bonus for sure. >> Appreciate it. >> All right, guys. >> Huh? >> I did. >> You guys guess what he wanted, but uh, no, he he said he just said good luck and and you know, everything. He was super supportive. It was good good to see him and and um you know he's he's uh he's uh he's had a good weekend. It's been really really fun to see him and and uh everybody's been really impressed. So um but yeah, he he uh he honestly he just showed his support.

title: Adam Peters Exclusive 2026 Draft Night Interview | Command Center | Washington Commanders | NFL
text: GM Adam Peters if you follow mock drafts but even over the last week there were about 18 different people that were linked to Washington. So this was an interesting draft and you ended up with Sunny Styles. At what point in the process did you kind of peg him as somebody that you'd like to be a commander? >> Yeah, really throughout the whole process he was always a guy that was on our radar. Uh he's he's a special kid. He's been on the radar for a long time. He was he was a big-time recruit. He was a safety that that uh moved a linebacker a couple years ago, but you had always seen him. You always knew who he was. Even three, four years ago, the the area scouts that are in there, they know who Sunonny Styles, you know, and they said, "That's Sunny Styles." And then you kind of watch him, he changed some numbers over the years, but um you know, he always stood out as an athlete. And then him becoming a linebacker the last couple of years, it was uh it was really cool to see the evolution. And then um there's just so much love for him in our building throughout the process, you know, starting with our first set of meetings uh with the college scouts and then with the coaches and then again as as we got into the draft meetings and then R&D is they love him and all his metrics and and everything and then obviously the combine to the combine and so you know the momentum grew and grew and grew and uh felt really great about it throughout the whole process until this last week. really um comfortable, you know, more than comfortable sitting there and taking him, but it was just a matter of was he going to be there? >> Yeah. >> Right. >> So, were you I mean, it sounds like cuz like Bram and I had a bet. He bet me a dollar that Sunny I said Sunny Sway he's going to be there. Bram's like he's going to be there. Were you surprised that he was there at seven for the pick >> a little bit? Yeah. I I thought um you know you know if you did the probability and and all that it it was not it was much more improbable than probable. So, and there was there's a lot of teams that were in front of us that I thought would would want them. And um so it's just the way the board fell. And then when when Kansas City traded up um you know, I I kind of figured they weren't trading up for for a linebacker. So um you know, I felt felt great there. >> You start smiling a little bit more. >> So So I played with Lorenzo's dad. I mean, I'm sorry, with Sunny's dad, Lorenzo Styles back in with the Rams. 99 Rams. We were we were teammates on the Super Bowl team. Um, and I text with Lorenzo over the last few uh couple years. And then recently after Sunny had that showing at the combine, I congratulated him on his son's showings and everything. And I was like, man, they crushed it. He's like, "Yeah, man. I would love, this was March 18th, he said, "Man, I would love for him to actually end up in Washington." And when he said that, I was like, "Yeah, I would love to be talking about." So, did you get to get the sense that he really wanted to be a commander during the process? >> Yeah, especially in the 30 visit, you could tell he expressed that and he expressed that to a lot of our coaches, too. And the feeling was mutual, you know. So, but um yeah, just uh he is he is what it means to be a commander. You know, he got our commander tag and and you know, through and through like it wasn't even a question. And so, um that part of it was easy. And uh that's cool that that that he's this day. >> I'll show you a text afterwards. >> He'll be here tomorrow. I'll be coming tomorrow. Yeah. So come come hang. Yeah. >> So another thing you mentioned about Sunny being a a safety at one point. Played two years a safety and then just two seasons as a linebacker. You saw his tape a year ago. Then this year I mean just the >> the ascend ascension of him at the position. Do you all still feel like I feel like he's just scratching the surface >> of his potential as a linebacker. Do you all kind of see his ceiling as through the roof? >> Yeah. I mean, he took the words right out of my mouth like he's got getting better and better. Even throughout this year, I I just said this to our our local press, but just throughout the year, he got better and better, and he's playing his best ball at the end of the year toward those late games and then the championship game and then in the playoffs. and so better at all those traits that you know that you you're talking about like whether it's playing in the box, whether it's blitzing, whe all the little nuances of the game and yeah, he's just scratching the surface. So, he's already a great player. I don't want to certainly take the way that he's a, you know, he's already great, but I think he's got another level. >> I want to ask you about evaluation when you have >> he had talented teammates with him. Two of them, one went right before him and one went right after him. All of them could have been top 10 picks. When you evaluate a player that has that kind of talent around them, how do you take into totality that group and the individual play that you watch from that one particular player? >> Yeah. One, it's really fun to watch. It's it's great. Like I watched every play of their defense and so it not not cuz I'm trying to be Mr. Hardo Scout, but like >> just fun. Like it was fun. And they're they have an outstanding coach. Matt Patricia is a great coach. you know, these guys have been coached really, really well. They're they're on the details. They understand their role in the defense. They communicate really well. So, you see that all coming together and everybody owning their role. And so, um, so it's it was just fun to watch. And so, I would lock in on say I'm watching their I'm watching Arll, but you you're locking in on him, but then you're kind of watching everybody else. And then I do one at a time. So, you watch it over and over. You watch a corner and they got a lot of guys on that defense. They're really good. And um obviously three, you know, guys who were almost top 10 picks and so um but you see, you know, as you're watching the other guys, you see Sunny flashing all the time and just how how big and long and fast he is. And so he's always jumping out at the tape, but certainly hats off to Matt Patricia and that defense and and it's fun. It's it's uh it's easy. It's an easy watch. Some of these aren't aren't that easy. That's an easy watch. >> You talked about the commander tag. Can you talk about like what goes into that formula of determining a commander a little bit? Obviously, like when you cut when you cut the film off, he's a physical freak, but I think it's cool that you guys identify the person as well, like what goes into that evaluation, you know, to get him here. >> Yeah. And that that's really our scouts. our scouts are digging in and all the work they put in really like I said I mean these guys have been watching him for a couple years and >> and then they go in and they get all the information on what type of person he is, the leader that he is, the communicator that he is, this quarterback of that defense and getting the guys lined up up front and so his football intelligence, his football character, all those different things that go into it and you know you you put a score on it, you know, you really and um and So he he he passed everything with flying colors, you know, in terms of all those things and and um you know, he's he's a team captain type. He he's all those things and and uh just an awesome guy off the field, too. When you um this is your third draft here as a general manager in Washington. First two years you're drafting for different type of offensive scheme, different type of defensive scheme. Now you got Donte Jones defense, you got David Blas offense. How was it going through that process with these guys kind trying to figure out, okay, what are they looking for in terms of what's the best type of uh player to fit their their um schemes and systems offensively and defensively? >> Yeah, it was really fun and those guys when they came in um they presented to all of us really the whole you know organization football side in terms of what we're looking for at each position, what how we're going to play offense, how we're going to play defense. And so those guys, you know, in that auditorium over there, they stood up and presented with clips and and went through position by position. So they painted a great picture for us. And then uh you know, both those guys have been excellent communicators and teachers and and so doors open go by and kind of just chop it up and say, "All right, um what do you think about this? What do you think about?" And so um not only do they present, but they're they're open at answering questions and and giving us examples. So that process has been really good. and they've been they were in the free agency meetings, they were in the draft meetings. Um so hearing them and their you know one their involvement, their buyin u in terms of our processes have been awesome and then their input in in teaching us like how how these guys fit, how Sunny will fit in the defense and and different guys like that. It's it's really been fun. Those guys are awesome. When you met with the media a week ago, you talked about all the signings that had occurred in free agency that didn't box you in to having to make a choice at a position. As this week progressed, were you leaning offense or defense or were you just going to wait and see how the board played out? >> Yeah, just wait and see how the board played out. Yeah, it was uh I think especially when you're when you're that high, you just get just get a great player. >> You know, you figure out the rest, you know, and uh I think we we did that. Yeah. >> Um so what's the next couple of days? cuz I know there's a long wait. Yeah. In between picks, but what are you looking for over the next couple of days? >> Um yeah, we we have the pick 71 um which is our only pick tomorrow and I think it'd be kind of tough to add another one at this point if we didn't do it with that pick. So um it's just waiting and and praying that our guys don't don't come off the board. But no, honestly, we'll get together and and just really go through the different iterations of all right, if not this, then this, and if these guys, these two guys are on the board, who we're picking, and hopefully there's a few guys to choose from where you can either just pick the best one or you can even trade down. So, just talking through those things beforehand. Um, kind of like we did with this pick, you know, we we we did all all kinds of exercises about trades and who could be there, who who not could be there, and then nobody called for the trade. So, all that work, we could have done something else, but but uh no, you have to you have to be ready for everything. And so, we'll do the same thing with that. Yeah. >> Uh you should have seen us after you guys made the pick. We were excited, too. We were very excited about the pick of Sunny Styles. Congratulations on the selection and good luck with the rest of the draft. Thanks so much. >> Yeah. Thanks, B. Thanks, guys. >> Cool. That awesome.
